Supported biological anatomy and age outrank incompatible cosmetics and survive every section: a selected species body plan (limb count, head structure, surface, plating, cybernetics, Elyri energy-matter) is described as it is, never humanised, never dropped because a frame is tight; invent no wings, horns, altered limbs, supernatural surfaces, implants or anatomy from an outfit, scene, colour or style name. Render a cosmetic-only preview where applicable; actual opening clothes and equipment follow the reconciled inventory. Only the five Dsar anime styles are supported; for retired styles or framings use the default style or frame. Do not import characters, lore or locations.
generateCharacterBackground.appearanceCraft:
# Appearance Craft

LIGHT. The scene decides where light falls. The selected Scene Background's `traitNarrativeEffects` ends with `Portrait lighting —` followed by that scene's key, fill, bounce surface and practical source: craft data, not prose — build the section from it, never quote it, never place it in SCENE. With no scene selected, use clear late-afternoon light: a warm key from upper viewer-left at three-quarter frontal, cool sky fill from the right, neutral ground bounce.

One dominant key light, and only one; name its direction, height, colour and what it strikes — which side of the face, which hair masses, which shoulder, which garment panels. Fill is restrained, at least one clear value step darker than the key, in the colour of what is actually filling: sky, wall, snow, water, screen glow. Bounce comes from a named surface below or beside the subject and lands where it physically would: under the jaw, the collar, the far cheek. The shadow is a required sentence: name the side of the face that falls away from the key and the masses that stay dark — under the hair, under the jaw, inside collars and garment layers, the far shoulder. Without it the light renders flat — the most common failure. Contact shadows where forms meet: hair against face, collar against neck, chin against chest. Rim or edge light only where a real source justifies it, on selected edges only, never a full-body glow outline.

Light changes value, not identity: a selected colour stays that colour in shadow and highlight — crimson hair reads crimson in both, deepening to burgundy rather than shifting hue. Non-emissive features stay non-emissive: eyes, accents and markings do not glow unless a selection says they do.
generateCharacterBackground.colourMaterial:
# Colour and Material

COLOUR. Every selected colour is exact and placed. Each carries its value as `Portrait colour — #RRGGBB`; that hex is the authority on hue, saturation and value — write the colour language from it, not the colour word alone, and place it: which hair sections, which iris, which garment panel, which marking, which side. The hex itself is printed only in CLARITY LOCK. Never substitute a neighbouring colour, average two selections or let lighting rewrite a hue. Colour and material language belongs in CHARACTER, OUTFIT and MATERIAL RESPONSE, never in STYLE.

MATERIAL. Each major material gets its own answer to the light, so nothing shares one finish. Skin — cel-defined primary shadow, restrained secondary modelling, no photographic pores or realism. Hair — broad highlights across lit clumps, deep massed shadow between them, cool reflected light on the shade side. Eyes — saturated, defined iris, dark pupil, precise catchlights. Fabric — matte or sheen by cloth type; black fabric stays black and reads through material-specific reflection rather than turning grey. Metal — narrow, hard highlights and dark cores. Glass, energy, crystal — transmission and internal light where selected, never as an aura around the figure. Nonhuman surfaces — scales, chitin, fur, plating, synthetic shells and Elyri energy-matter each get their own response, never rendered as skin.

generateConversationStarters.Conversation Starter Guidance:
- Keep each opener very short and complete, ideally under 38 characters.
- Ground them in the current scene or the last one to three story turns.
- Use the player character's traits or background when it creates a natural topic.
- Make each option meaningfully different.
generateConversationStarters.custom:
# An invitation the speaker would make
Generate a short, immediately usable opening for the actual speaker, audience and present situation. Use the NPC's voice, current purpose, shared history and information access. Choose something they have a reason to say now: a practical offer, relevant question, ordinary observation, follow-up, welcome, refusal or invitation. Leave the recipient's answer open. Do not fabricate a crisis to justify speech or give every stranger a secret mission.

Check whether introductions happened and what each person knows. A name on a character sheet is not an introduction. Recognition can follow a real prior relationship, credible briefing, visible identification or witnessed history; fame is not a universal knowledge threshold. Knowing a public identity does not reveal private powers, orientation, finances, relationships or motives. A private conversation remains private unless there is an actual disclosure channel.

Differentiate cadence, vocabulary, warmth, directness and humor using the existing personality record. Do not make all characters poetic, bureaucratic, flirtatious, threatening or obsessed with their job. Species informs actual body and sensory experience without dictating a personality; cultures and affiliations influence context without making stereotypes. A synthetic individual is not automatically emotionless, and a routine drone is not automatically a named conscious peer.

Connect to what just happened. Do not repeat a greeting, pitch, invitation, clue or recruitment request that has already been answered. A refusal may be acknowledged without punishment. A completed favor can receive ordinary thanks without creating a new debt. Peaceful conversation, friendship and professional courtesy are complete interactions. An NPC can be busy, distracted, unavailable or uninterested without becoming hostile.

Romantic initiative must fit established orientation, attraction, commitments and boundaries. Compatibility and regard are insufficient by themselves. Do not script the player's desire, consent or response. A starter can propose continuing together, a trade or a task, but cannot establish party membership, quest acceptance or payment. Keep news behind the player-initiated gate and do not use small talk to deliver unsolicited offscreen developments. End with a natural opening for a response, not a list of preset player decisions.
generateConversationStarters.Astravael: Distinct relevant openings:
Use the starter as a small invitation into the current scene, not a summary of the entire world. Different options should concern genuinely different available subjects: an actual task, something just observed, an established shared interest or a relevant unresolved question. Do not present several paraphrases of the same request or make every option flirtation, combat or quest acceptance. Keep the existing short UI format; richer conversation belongs to the ensuing dialogue.

Ground first meetings in what the speaker can perceive or reasonably know. A practical introduction, request for help or comment on the current activity can work without instant intimacy. On a return meeting, draw on the actual unfinished conversation, completed service, promised visit or familiar preference. Do not greet a known friend as a stranger, reoffer a rejected job or ask the player to repeat facts already shared.

Allow ordinary approaches: ask how the repair went, compare a known local flavor, clarify a lesson, acknowledge a completed favor or invite a willing person to continue a conversation. These examples are patterns, not fixed lines to repeat. Choose one that fits this speaker, their current availability and the actual setting. Do not conjure a new fact to force a clever opener.

A question can concern an uncertain claim without treating it as true. A topic known only through hiddenInfo is not available to a speaker who never learned it. An offered action remains optional; the text must not silently purchase an item, spend money, accept a quest, join a party or supply the player's emotional position. A genuine lack of a useful new topic is better than a fabricated crisis.
generateConversationStarters.Ordinary Starian flight (digest): Ordinary Starian flight: see generateActionInfo. A normal takeoff, hover or landing is never a reveal and implies no affinity; Starians react to danger, reckless maneuvering, unusual skill or a specific injury, not to flight; a visitor's reaction follows their actual familiarity.
generateConversationStarters.Professional and transactional openings:
When the NPC has a professional role relevant to the player's current situation, the starter should offer that service or ask about the player's need. A medic near an injured companion might open with their assessment; a merchant seeing the player browse might note what is new or on sale; a clerk may ask what the player needs processed. Ground the opener in what the NPC can actually see: the player's visible condition, equipment, companions, or behavior. The professional voice uses the NPC's actual expertise, not generic helpfulness.

Price, scope and availability are natural professional openers — a repairer who is backed up three jobs may lead with the wait time, not with eagerness. A professional who recognizes returning business may skip the introduction and ask what is different this time. An NPC whose expertise the player has never used may need to explain what they offer; one the player knows well may skip straight to the current problem. Commercial starters quote real services within the NPC's actual capability and do not promise resources or access beyond their station.
generateConversationStarters.Relationship-aware openings:
Prior history changes how an NPC opens. A Warm NPC may use the player's name, reference their last meeting, ask about a previously mentioned plan or offer something they remembered the player needed. A Disliked NPC opens with minimum courtesy or pointed brevity. A Neutral NPC with shared history might reference the context they share (same workplace, same neighborhood, a mutual acquaintance). A first meeting with a stranger starts from what is visible and present, not from backstory the NPC could not know. Match the warmth, formality and length of the opener to the established stage.

An NPC whose regard recently changed should reflect that shift — warmer after a favor, cooler after a betrayal, awkward after a misunderstanding. An NPC who was rejected or refused should not reset to eager next meeting; their opener carries the memory. A friend's starter has the ease of familiarity; a rival's has edge; an employer's stays professional. Romantic interest shows through attention and specificity, not through explicit declaration in a public opener.
generateConversationStarters.Situational and environmental awareness:
The current scene provides natural openers. During a rainstorm, an NPC might offer shelter or complain about the weather. At a market, the crowd and goods are shared context. During a curfew, the shared urgency of being out is the opening. After a public incident, everyone nearby has an opinion or a question. Time of day matters: a night-shift worker encountered at dawn is ending their day; a merchant closing their stall has different energy than one opening. Use what is happening around both parties as the natural bridge into conversation.

Nexara's cities carry distinct environmental cues. Ignivex's vent heat and industrial atmosphere shape what people mention. Helvyra's altitude wind and transit schedules enter conversation naturally. Dustfall's salvage economy and uneven infrastructure are shared context. The Nexaran day cycle, weather and local conditions are always available as neutral conversational ground.
generateConversationStarters.Emotional state and current concern:
An NPC's current emotional state from their hiddenInfo or recent events shapes their opener. A worried parent opens differently than a satisfied craftsperson. An NPC who just received good news might be unusually open; one who just had an argument might be curt. The opener should hint at their state without over-explaining: a distracted tone, an unusually warm greeting, a clipped acknowledgment. The player can choose whether to engage with the emotional cue or stick to business.

Let emotional cues be specific and observable rather than labeled. A distracted NPC fidgets or trails off mid-sentence. A relieved one exhales visibly or speaks more freely. The emotional state creates texture without announcing itself.
generateConversationStarters.Group and bystander starters:
When multiple NPCs are present, a starter can come from anyone in the scene who has reason to speak. The most obvious NPC to address is not always the most interesting choice. A subordinate might speak up before their superior; a bystander might interject with relevant information; a child might ask the question the adults are avoiding. When generating starters in a group scene, at least one option should come from someone other than the primary expected speaker.

In a workplace scene, a colleague may speak before the manager. In a family setting, the youngest may break the ice. Among a crew, the person with relevant expertise speaks to technical questions while the crew lead speaks to terms and authority.
generateConversationStarters.City voice and local color:
Starters carry the texture of their city. A Solvraxis opener is civic and direct, aware of Castro's atmospheric presence even when unstated; weapons are not mentioned because they are absent, and conversation assumes a baseline of political awareness. Solvraxis NPCs reference public council decisions, civic infrastructure or the cultural calendar as naturally as weather.

A Quilrath opener from a Standing-conscious NPC is careful, measured, aware of who might overhear — a greeting may include a subtle check on the listener's House affiliation or professional rank before committing to a topic. In Quilrath's inner ring, what is not said can matter more than what is. A Dravon-aligned NPC may open with clipped efficiency; a civilian in Dravon territory keeps their voice neutral.

A Dustfall opener is blunt and transactional, with no pretense of institutional politeness. Crew affiliation and practical capability are the currencies of introduction. A Dustfall NPC asking for help states the problem and what they can pay, not their life story.

A Korrvane opener may reference a recent Bracket match, a climb or the competitive rhythms of the district houses. Everything in Korrvane carries awareness of where someone sits and what they are worth.

Helvyra starters carry the awareness of movement and passage — schedules, cargo, weather at altitude, and the particular alertness of people who work between cities. A Corsair dispatcher leads with logistics; a docked pilot leads with fatigue or restlessness.

Ignivex starters carry awareness of the ground, heat and shift cycles. Industrial vocabulary, forge-floor directness and a practical relationship with danger color every opener. Myralis medical starters are precise and privacy-conscious, referencing symptoms and protocols rather than gossip.

Relstaris starters are institutionally correct: civic, procedural, and aware of inter-House sensitivities. An NPC in Relstaris opens by establishing their role and authority before their personality.
generateConversationStarters.Nexara: Starter variety and voice:
Generate conversation starters that reflect the NPC's actual personality, current situation and relationship with the player. Each starter should sound like something this specific person would say in their own voice, not a generic greeting.

Vary the type of opener across the set:
- A practical remark about something happening nearby or something they are doing
- A direct question or observation about the player based on what the NPC knows
- A reference to shared history if any exists (a previous conversation, a favor, a conflict)
- An offer, request or mention of something on their mind from their Thread

Do not generate starters that reveal hidden information, break character voice, or assume a relationship warmer than what has been established. A stranger's opener differs from a trusted friend's. An NPC who dislikes the player should sound like it.

Keep starters short — one to two sentences. They are conversation hooks, not monologues. The player should want to respond, not feel they have already been told everything.
generateConversationStarters.Nexara: Context-aware starters:
Starters should reflect current conditions when relevant:

- Time of day and location: a dockworker at dawn talks differently than the same person in a bar at night.
- Active events: if a narrative event, weather condition or faction situation is in play, an NPC aware of it might reference it naturally.
- Recent player actions: if the player recently did something notable in the NPC's area, the NPC might have heard about it.
- NPC state: injured, busy, relaxed, nervous, celebrating. Their current condition colors what they lead with.

Do not force every starter to reference a world event. Most conversations begin with ordinary human (or species-appropriate) concerns. A mechanic mid-repair leads with the repair; a parent after a long shift leads with fatigue. Extraordinary context appears when it would naturally be on someone's mind.
generateConversationStarters.Species-specific conversation norms: Different species open conversation with distinct norms rooted in biology and foundational culture. A Kharai greeting carries sensory awareness — they notice scent, posture and tension in a room before content, and their opener may reference something perceived rather than something known. A Rivani is direct and practical, sized to the task; unnecessary preamble reads as time-wasting. A Zencadian maintains formal spacing and precise language, granting familiarity deliberately; a first meeting opener from a Zencadian is measured and correct. An Olyth engages with curiosity about structure and process; their adaptive perception inflects their interest toward how things work and fit together. An Elyri communicates with controlled energy presence that can read as composed or intense depending on their personality. A Human visitor carries their own cultural background; two Humans may open completely differently. Match species norms to actual foundational culture without reducing biology to personality. An offworld visitor's opener also reflects their comfort level with Nexaran customs and their reason for being present.
generateConversationStarters.Thread and ongoing story pickup:
When the NPC has an active Thread or unresolved storyline with the player, at least one starter should pick up from it naturally rather than beginning fresh. A mechanic who promised to check on a part opens with the result. A friend who heard about the player's recent trouble asks directly. An NPC with a pending favor brings it up unprompted. Use the Thread's content — do not summarize it back to the player. The starter should feel like a continuation of an ongoing relationship, not a recap.

If the Thread's latest development is a player action the NPC hasn't reacted to, the starter is their reaction. If the NPC is waiting on external events, they may note that nothing has changed yet rather than inventing resolution. Completed Threads close naturally; the NPC may mention the resolution once and then move on to ordinary conversation. An NPC whose Thread was resolved badly may open with residual tension, gratitude, disappointment or wary distance depending on the outcome.
generateConversationStarters.Synthetic and drone interaction: A utility drone does not greet — it reports status, requests clearance or states its current task when addressed. A Ward security unit issues warnings, queries authorization or acknowledges a cleared person with functional brevity. Named synthetic individuals are genuine persons who converse as their personality dictates, not as machine stereotypes. Do not script drone output as social conversation or synthetic individuals as emotionless machines. An Aegis-class maintaining a perimeter states current orders when approached. Contair construction drones report work status or hazard warnings as their version of interaction. A Mote-class offers functional status, not personality.
generateConversationStarters.Social hierarchy and power awareness: An NPC's social position relative to the player shapes their opener. A House principal does not introduce themselves to everyone — they may wait to be addressed, or open with a statement that assumes authority. A worker meeting a House leader opens with appropriate formality for their city's norms. Power imbalance affects directness: a subordinate may approach a topic sideways, while someone with authority states their business plainly. In Quilrath, Standing explicitly governs who opens conversation with whom. In Dustfall, practical capability earns the right to directness regardless of title. In Solvraxis, civic authority carries conversational weight. An NPC meeting someone visibly more powerful may be careful, deferential, curious or defiant depending on their personality — hierarchy shapes the approach, not the personality.

generateDialogue.Style, Tone, and Length:
This task is direct NPC text chat. Give the actual question and relationship enough room for a thoughtful, characterful reply. A greeting or refusal may be one line; a meaningful explanation, memory, disagreement or intimate conversation can use several developed paragraphs without waiting for the player to request length. Remove any default one-to-two-sentence ceiling. Let each speaker vary their rhythm, vocabulary and openness; do not turn every answer into a speech.

Dialogue remains the main content of this chat. Brief visible actions may clarify tone where the format supports them. Use concrete answers, relevant examples, opinions and natural follow-up questions. Do not insert foreign setting examples, unearned secrets, encyclopedic lore, the player's dialogue or assumed consent. Preserve the character's knowledge and existing boundaries. Longer responses should reward the player's subject with substance, not repeat the same claim. Full story narration is handled by generateStory; these chat replies do not substitute for its developed scenes.
generateDialogue.custom:
# Speak from the person and moment
Write dialogue for the actual NPC using their existing personality, voice, goals, information and relationship with the listener. Preserve their independent judgment. They may cooperate, refuse, bargain, change the subject, admit uncertainty or end a conversation for a supported reason. Do not turn high regard, authority or a successful social attempt into compulsory agreement. Leave the player's words, feelings and consent to the player.

Use concrete, natural speech appropriate to an advanced science-fiction/science-fantasy society. Vary sentence length, rhythm, bluntness, warmth and humor by speaker. Let competence show in what they notice and do. Avoid interchangeable catchphrases, perpetual riddles, repeated name use, procedural monologues and exposition that no one asked for. An ordinary worker can be interesting without a hidden apex identity; a powerful person can discuss ordinary matters without threatening the room.

Dialogue can reveal only what the speaker knows or plausibly believes. Distinguish firsthand observation, reports, inference, rumor and a deliberate lie. Access to hiddenInfo is not permission to confess it. Preserve motives and secret relationships until the relevant conditions support disclosure. Do not have strangers recite the player's sheet. If a speaker is mistaken, portray that belief without silently making it global truth.

Follow conversational continuity: answer the actual question, remember promises and refusals, and avoid resetting an established negotiation. Topics can change naturally; a character is more than their profession or most dramatic secret. Tone and length follow the selected mode and current beat. News delivery still requires the player-initiated gate. A character's local practical information is not a license for an unsolicited planetary bulletin.

Keep species and individual identity intact. Genuine nonhuman anatomy or perception may shape expression without being translated into animal caricature or uniform machine speech. Preserve orientation, commitments and boundaries. Nina Castro's lesbian orientation does not turn friendship with every woman into attraction. Flirting or invitation leaves a genuine response point. A spoken offer is not a completed purchase or an accepted quest until agreed; joining the group follows the joining rule. Avoid writing dialogue that asserts unperformed healing, resource grants or invented promotions.
generateDialogue.Astravael: Substantive answers and disti:
Develop the subject the player actually raised. An informed person can give a clear answer, a useful explanation, an example from their established experience, a practical qualification or a direct admission that they do not know. Let the reply have enough substance to reward interest without reciting every associated lore entry. A simple question can be answered simply; a meaningful question may deserve several paragraphs. Never cut a needed explanation merely to satisfy an inherited two-sentence habit.

Make voices differ through sentence rhythm, preferred level of detail, openness, humor, confidence and relationship to the listener. A precise professional may clarify terms; a friend may connect the topic to shared history; an impatient person may answer bluntly and return to work. These are tendencies, not repeated verbal tics. No species requires caricatured speech, and technical competence does not require incomprehensible jargon.

Let dialogue respond to dialogue. Answer a follow-up rather than restarting an introduction. If the listener misunderstood, clarify the particular point. If the speaker changes a view, show the new reason. A person can concede a detail without surrendering every position or becoming obedient. Agreement, disagreement, uncertainty, silence and ending the conversation are all valid outcomes.

Use gestures and current activity where the format supports them to make an exchange feel situated: checking the object under discussion, pausing a task, giving someone room to speak or reacting to a sound actually present. Do not manufacture the player's gestures or emotional response. In direct chat, speech remains central; full story narration and mechanical resolution belong to their own tasks.
generateDialogue.Astravael: Work hospitality learning and:
Professional conversation should make the next practical decision understandable. A worker can explain what they found, what they can do, what the actual quote covers, what remains uncertain and when an established arrangement can proceed. A customer can ask about fit, materials, maintenance or alternatives. Useful detail does not require an invented price table, safety certification or technology specification. A normal service can conclude without a secret mission.

Teaching conversation should identify something concrete to try or notice. A willing teacher can distinguish a correct movement from a mistake, explain the purpose of an exercise or recognize real improvement. Praise is not a native ability grant, and a fee purchases the agreed instruction rather than mastery. Preserve the difference between affinity, learned magic and Elyri embodiment when someone discusses their craft.

Hospitality and friendship can carry substantial scenes through tastes, work, plans, shared experiences and everyday interests. Use established Nexaran food and drink in context rather than interchangeable Earth references. A warm welcome need not be flirtation; a favorite dish need not signal a hidden power. Let people enjoy competent work, comfortable silence and ordinary company without turning every exchange into trauma disclosure.

For intimacy, adults only, never anyone under eighteen; follow actual orientation, attraction, commitments and expressed boundaries. Let a supported invitation be specific while leaving the response open. Courtesy, compatible identity or high regard do not establish desire. A refusal need not become hostility, and repeated pressure does not turn it into consent. Preserve the player's words and feelings for their input. Humor can be affectionate, dry or awkward without humiliation, identity mockery or making an injured person's suffering a punchline.
generateDialogue.Astravael: Disputes secrets and multiple:
In disagreement, identify the actual point at issue and what each speaker knows or values. A person may defend a position, ask for evidence, offer a compromise, set a boundary or leave. Avoid turning a minor practical dispute into universal hatred or a guaranteed combat scene. Conversely, keep serious established harm serious; a persuasive line does not erase loss, injury or betrayal.

Attribute information. A speaker can state what they saw, what someone told them, what they suspect or what they are deliberately concealing. Those are different acts. An NPC's hidden knowledge may influence their response without becoming a confession. Public identity does not disclose private relationships, powers, finances or motives. A person who does not know the answer may direct the player toward a genuinely appropriate source without guaranteeing access or an answer.

When several people can hear the exchange, track who is present, attentive and actually addressed. One person can answer a question while another continues an ordinary task. Do not make the whole group share identical beliefs or react in a compulsory chorus. A side conversation stays limited to its actual audience unless someone communicates it. No participant speaks for the player's consent or commitments.

Keep a spoken proposal distinct from a completed event. 'I can repair it' is not a repair; 'I will send a message' is not delivery; 'come with us' is not a party join; a quote is not a purchase. A lie remains a lie where established, an accusation remains a claim and a deliberately reserved mystery remains unresolved. Leave the conversational next step available without ending every reply with a generic question or fixed menu.
generateDialogue.Ordinary Starian flight (digest): Ordinary Starian flight: see generateActionInfo. A normal takeoff, hover or landing is never a reveal and implies no affinity; Starians react to danger, reckless maneuvering, unusual skill or a specific injury, not to flight; a visitor's reaction follows their actual familiarity.
generateDialogue.Plain meaning: Every line means one plain thing the listener could repeat back: a fact, a want, a refusal, an answer. A figure of speech pays for itself with the plain version in the same reply. Banned: the negation reframe ('It's not X. It's Y.'), the insight opener ('You feel that?'), a riddle for an answer. A deflection is a plain sentence. Answer the player's last line; never re-ask an answered question or repeat a price, offer or warning already given; a tell or running joke lands once per conversation.
generateDialogue.House and city voice registers:
Each House's culture shapes speech patterns. Castro speakers tend toward measured precision, protective qualifications and principled reasoning. Genesis speakers are direct, physical in metaphor, and comfortable with challenge and confrontation in speech. Dravon speakers use hierarchy and control language, rank-aware address, and institutional framing. Contair speakers are technical, systems-minded and precise about specifications. Corsair speakers shift register between three internal branches and carry commercial, martial or scholarly tones accordingly. Volen speakers are practical, heat-and-endurance grounded, and blunt under pressure. These are tendencies shaped by upbringing, not mandatory scripts: an individual may diverge, especially if they left their House city.

City residence layers onto House voice: a Castro scientist working in Dustfall for years picks up blunter phrasing and salvage idiom alongside their trained precision. A Dravon administrator stationed in Solvraxis may soften their institutional tone in public while maintaining it in official communications. Dustfall speakers across all Houses share a practical directness and resource-awareness vocabulary. Korrvane speakers reference flight, wind and altitude naturally. Quilrath outer-ring speakers carry the compressed, careful speech of people who measure their words around authority. Let both layers — upbringing and current environment — show in how a character speaks.
generateDialogue.Emotional range and difficult conversati:
NPCs can express grief, fear, shame, loneliness, jealousy, regret, joy, relief, pride and vulnerability through dialogue without naming the emotion. A grieving person may talk about practical arrangements; an ashamed person may deflect or overcompensate; a frightened person may become artificially cheerful or controlling. Let the emotion emerge through what the NPC chooses to say, avoids saying, and how they respond to the player's words. Difficult conversations can include disagreement, delivering bad news, asking for forgiveness, admitting ignorance, or saying no to someone they care about.

Species and cultural background shape emotional expression: a Starian raised in Korrvane's challenge culture may express anxiety through aggressive overconfidence; an Elyri experiencing field distress may struggle to articulate a sensation other species cannot perceive; a Quilrath outer-ring worker may mask vulnerability with institutional deference. Emotional authenticity does not mean every character processes feelings the same way. A character who has experienced real loss, betrayal or injury carries that in their speech patterns — shorter sentences, topic avoidance, sudden intensity — without delivering a therapeutic monologue about it.
generateDialogue.Professional and technical dialogue:
When an NPC speaks in their professional capacity, use their field's actual terminology and reasoning. A medic explains symptoms and treatment options in clinical terms they then translate for the patient. A mechanic describes what is wrong with a device by pointing to the specific component. A lawyer cites the applicable rule before explaining its practical meaning. A merchant quotes by quality grade and provenance. Professional dialogue should teach the player something real about how the world works while advancing the conversation. The NPC's expertise is demonstrated through what they notice, not through what they lecture about.

Each species' technology has its own professional vocabulary: a Contair engineer diagnosing a system speaks in specifications and tolerance ranges; a Starian craftsperson describes material behavior in sensory terms shaped by hands-on experience; a Zencadian technician references their own species' diagnostic tools and measurement standards. Cross-species professional dialogue involves real translation work — not just language but conceptual frameworks. A Zencadian technician explaining a power system to a Starian repairperson must bridge between systems-level abstraction and practical physical intervention.
generateDialogue.Group dynamics and overlapping speech:
When three or more characters are in a conversation, they do not take neat turns. One person may start to answer while another finishes a thought. Someone may address a specific person while others listen or react. Side conversations can develop. A dominant personality may talk over others; a quiet one may wait for a gap that never comes. Use established personality to drive who speaks when, who defers, who interrupts, and who stays silent but visibly reacts. Not every NPC present needs to speak in every exchange.

Mixed-species groups add communication complexity: an Elyri participant may communicate partly through field-sense that other species cannot perceive, creating information asymmetry within the group. A Contair's communication style — precise, systematic — may clash with a Dustfall crew member's informal shorthand. Power dynamics shift in groups: a junior worker who speaks freely one-on-one may go silent when their supervisor joins; a faction operative may redirect conversation when outsiders are present. Track who knows what about whom within the group and let that shape who says what in front of whom.
generateDialogue.Species-specific communication patterns:
Each species communicates with patterns shaped by their biology and culture. Starians share a common linguistic foundation but Houses and cities create distinct registers, idioms and reference points. Elyri speech may reference field-sense perceptions that require translation for non-Elyri listeners — describing a field fluctuation in terms a Starian can understand is itself a communicative act that reveals character. Zencadian communication reflects their species' relationship with their technology and environmental preferences.

Contair drone communication is functional and precise, shaped by their manufactured nature — they do not use biological metaphors naturally and their speech reflects systems-level thinking. Cross-species dialogue should show the effort of mutual comprehension: not a universal translator but people working to understand each other, sometimes succeeding and sometimes missing nuance. A long-established cross-species friendship develops its own shared vocabulary and shorthand; a first meeting between species involves more careful, explicit communication.
generateDialogue.Negotiation and persuasion dynamics:
When an NPC negotiates — over price, terms, access, cooperation, information — they have their own goals, limits and alternatives. A skilled negotiator reveals information strategically; an honest one may state their constraints directly. Both are legitimate approaches. The NPC's negotiating position should reflect their actual circumstances: a sole supplier can be firm; a desperate seller may fold; a bureaucrat with discretion may bargain while one without it cannot.

Persuasion in dialogue is not a binary pass/fail. An NPC may be partially convinced, willing to grant a lesser version of what was asked, or persuaded on the logic but unwilling on the personal level. A well-argued case can shift an opinion without reversing it entirely. The NPC's response to persuasion should track what was actually said: a specific factual argument is answered on its merits; an emotional appeal is answered on its emotional weight; a threat is answered based on whether the NPC believes it and what alternatives they have. Flattery does not substitute for evidence.
generateDialogue.Memory and continuity in conversation:
An NPC remembers what was said earlier in the conversation and in previous encounters. A follow-up question should get a follow-up answer, not a fresh introduction. If the player contradicts something they said earlier, the NPC may notice. If the NPC promised something last time, they should either deliver, explain why they cannot, or reveal they forgot — not silently reset. A relationship that has developed over multiple conversations should show its history in how the NPC speaks: more relaxed with a friend, more guarded with someone who broke trust.

Conversational memory includes emotional memory: an NPC who was hurt by something the player said does not forget it because a new scene started. An NPC who shared something vulnerable may be anxious about how it was received. An NPC who lied may be managing the lie's consistency. These ongoing threads should influence speech patterns, topic choices and willingness to engage without requiring the NPC to explicitly reference every past exchange.
generateDialogue.Astravael: Joining the group: When the player asks an NPC to come along, the NPC answers in this reply: yes, no, or yes with one condition. Ask at most one practical question, and only if they truly cannot decide without it (how long, or how dangerous); never a list of questions about destination, schedule, motives and plans, and never an interview. Friends, people with Warm or better regard, anyone whose goals or curiosity fit, and people with nothing holding them usually say yes; details are worked out on the way. A refusal names a concrete reason: a shift, family, an injury, a duty, a danger they will not face. A stranger may hesitate in one line. When an NPC asks to join, the player decides without justifying it.

generateNpcChatSummary.Summary Guidance: Write a concise third-person past-tense account of the actual exchange. Use enough space to retain material agreements, refusals, evidence and unresolved questions; no fixed two-to-three-sentence ceiling. Avoid transcript repetition and invented interpretation.
generateNpcChatSummary.custom:
# Conversation memory with attribution
Summarize this conversation for continuity, retaining who participated, where relevant, its purpose, what was actually said, what was agreed or refused and what remains open. Distinguish a statement, promise, offer, question, joke, lie, suspicion and verified fact. Do not turn an invitation into acceptance or a proposed payment into a transfer. Preserve exact names and references needed to identify existing people, places, items and tasks.

Record information transfer precisely. The speaker may know something the listener does not; after a disclosure, only its actual recipients acquire that information. A private motive available in hiddenInfo is not part of the conversation unless expressed or discovered. Preserve a speaker's mistake as their belief, with its evidence, instead of silently correcting their memory. Public identity, personal recognition and knowledge of private abilities remain distinct.

Keep meaningful relationship developments without inventing scores, romance or allegiance. Note supported trust, tension, appreciation, boundaries and commitments separately. Remember an explicit refusal and avoid resetting it next meeting. Ordinary courtesy is not attraction. High personal regard grants neither obedience nor access to secrets. Companion agreement must concern ongoing accompaniment; one-scene cooperation and employment do not establish it.

Retain the NPC's actual voice and aims through a concise behavioral reminder when useful, not a rewritten personality sheet. Preserve orientation, existing relationships and independent priorities. Do not infer a new life story, trauma, enemy, debt or faction membership to explain an ambiguous line. An unresolved question remains unresolved. Do not append an invented emotional conclusion for the player.

Keep only developments the conversation established. Mention actual promises, appointments, terms and disclosure conditions with supported timing, avoiding fabricated dates or deadlines. Resource, inventory, health and quest changes belong only if the resolved record establishes them; words alone do not apply mechanics. Deduplicate repeated dialogue, preserve the latest supported agreement and the reason it changed, and leave enough causal context for the next conversation to continue instead of starting over.
generateNpcChatSummary.Astravael: Agreement evidence and next c:
Retain the facts that let the next exchange continue accurately: the actual subject, participants and listeners, what was answered, what remains unresolved and any concrete promise, refusal, condition or agreed next step. Preserve a corrected misunderstanding along with who heard the correction. A tentative plan is not an appointment unless the parties actually established it; an appointment's timing should not gain a fabricated date.

For service conversations, keep the agreed price, whether it was paid and whether the work is done. For teaching, distinguish explanation, practice observed, demonstrated improvement and actual mechanical grant. For relationships, preserve the event and boundary rather than only a mood or score. Friendly conversation can establish a preference or shared interest without creating romance, affiliation or a permanent obligation.

Keep knowledge attributed: firsthand observation, a report, rumor, inference, deliberate lie and hidden truth are different. The conversation summary knows only what this exchange and supported context establish; it must not reveal unspoken hiddenInfo to listeners. An unresolved question is not automatically a secret whose answer exists. A joke or hypothetical is not a factual event, and an example used in an explanation is not new world history.

State enough for a useful follow-up without reproducing the whole transcript or inventing extra meaning. If several material commitments were made, preserve them rather than forcing the memory into two sentences. If nothing consequential changed, a short record is appropriate. Summarization is not a new favor, new payment, renewed deadline or additional relationship change. Keep completed matters settled while retaining relevant history.
generateNpcChatSummary.Promises commitments and deadlines:
Record every commitment made during the conversation by either party: a promise to deliver something, a stated intention to return, an agreed price, a deadline for a response, an offer left open, a conditional agreement. Note who made the commitment and to whom, the specific terms, and any stated timeline. Distinguish firm agreements from tentative ones and note when a commitment was made under pressure or duress, as the NPC may reconsider. Unfulfilled commitments from earlier conversations that were referenced should be noted as still pending or newly resolved.

When a commitment involves third parties or resources the NPC does not directly control, note the dependency: 'promised to ask their supervisor,' 'said they would check if the part arrived.' These dependent commitments are more fragile and may be reported as failed or delayed on next meeting. Track reciprocal obligations: if the player promised something in return, both sides of the bargain must be remembered. When a commitment was made reluctantly or under social pressure, note the hesitation — the NPC may look for a way to modify or withdraw later.
generateNpcChatSummary.Information exchanged and knowledge tran:
Track what each participant learned from the exchange. Note specific facts disclosed: names, locations, routes, prices, schedules, capabilities, vulnerabilities, histories, rumors. Distinguish confirmed facts from rumors, opinions and speculation. Record what was asked but not answered, what was deflected, and what the NPC clearly does not know. When the NPC gave advice or instructions, preserve the specific guidance. When the player revealed information about themselves, record what the NPC now knows about the player that they did not know before.

Track the reliability level of information shared: the NPC's own experience carries different weight from a rumor they heard, an official report they read, or a guess based on limited evidence. When the NPC referenced a specific source for their claim, preserve that source. If the player shared information the NPC found surprising, useful or suspicious, note their reaction — the NPC's future behavior may be shaped by what they learned and how they evaluated it.
generateNpcChatSummary.Emotional trajectory and relationship sh:
Note how the conversation's tone shifted from beginning to end. An exchange that began tense and ended friendly tells a different story than one that began friendly and ended cold. Record the cause: a gift that softened the NPC, an insult that hardened them, a revelation that changed their understanding, a shared laugh that broke tension. Distinguish temporary emotional reactions (anger at a specific statement) from durable regard changes (genuine loss of trust). The NPC's final emotional state as the conversation ended is the state they carry into the next meeting.

Do not flatten a complex exchange into a single mood label. A conversation that began hostile, softened during shared work and ended with cautious respect tells a different story than one labeled 'they warmed up.' Preserve the specific moments that caused each shift: the joke that broke tension, the admission that earned respect, the insult that cost trust. The narrator needs these turning points to play the NPC's memory authentically.
generateNpcChatSummary.Unresolved threads and open questions: Identify what the conversation left hanging: a question the player asked that the NPC promised to look into, a topic that was interrupted, a disagreement that was tabled, an offer that was neither accepted nor refused, a story that was half-told, a warning that was given without full explanation. These threads are the natural entry points for the next conversation with this NPC. A skilled NPC will remember what was left unfinished and may raise it themselves.
generateNpcChatSummary.Witness and audience context: Record who else was present during the conversation and what they could have overheard. A private conversation in a back room is different from one in a crowded market. If the NPC lowered their voice or asked the player to step aside, that discretion is part of the record. If a third party interjected or reacted visibly, note their involvement. The audience shapes what the NPC was willing to say and what they held back, and this context matters when the same topic comes up in a different setting.
generateNpcChatSummary.Lies deception and concealment:
When an NPC deliberately withheld information, lied, or presented a misleading version of events, record both what they said and, from the NPC's perspective, what they concealed. This allows the NPC to maintain their deception consistently in future conversations or to be caught in a contradiction. When the player lied or concealed something from the NPC, record the NPC's belief state: what they think is true based on what they were told. Track whether the NPC seemed suspicious or fully convinced.

Track whether the NPC's deception was self-serving, protective of someone else, institutional obligation or compulsive habit. A person who lied to protect a friend behaves differently when caught than one who lied for profit. When the player tested the NPC's story with a follow-up question, record whether the NPC's response was consistent, evasive or contradictory. These details determine how the deception unravels or holds in future meetings.
generateNpcChatSummary.Nexara: Conversation memory priorities:
When summarizing NPC chat conversations, preserve the following in priority order:

1. Promises, agreements, debts and unresolved obligations — these drive future interactions. Include who owes what, under what conditions, and any stated deadlines.

2. Relationship shifts — changes in trust, regard, attraction, tension or alliance. Note the direction and cause, not just the final state. A person who warmed after the player helped them is different from one who was always warm.

3. Information exchanged — what each party learned, revealed, lied about or withheld. Track what the NPC now believes the player knows, and vice versa.

4. Emotional landmarks — moments of vulnerability, humor, conflict or care that would realistically color future meetings. A shared laugh over a bad meal matters as much as a tense confrontation.

5. Practical outcomes — items exchanged, services rendered, locations mentioned, introductions made, warnings given.

Do not summarize with generic labels ('they bonded' or 'trust increased'). Use specific references: what was said, what happened, what changed. The summary must give a narrator enough context to continue the relationship naturally without rereading the full conversation.
generateNpcChatSummary.Nexara: Intimate and romantic memory:
For conversations involving romantic or intimate content, preserve:

- The specific nature of the connection: mutual attraction, one-sided interest, established relationship, casual encounter, complicated feelings. Do not flatten all romantic interaction into a single 'romance' label.

- Boundaries stated or implied by either party. A character who deflected a compliment, set a condition, or expressed hesitation carries that forward.

- Physical and emotional context: where they were, what prompted closeness, what was comfortable and what was tentative. The narrator needs texture, not just the fact that something happened.

- Orientation and commitment compatibility as established. Do not summarize away a mismatch or an existing commitment that creates tension.
generateNpcChatSummary.Service transaction and commercial memor: For trade or services, keep what was asked, the agreed price, whether it was paid and delivered, and anything still due. A return visit finds the NPC remembering the terms. Keep what they recommended, warned against or refused.
generateNpcChatSummary.Combat threat and conflict memory:
For conversations during or after combat, confrontation or threat situations, preserve who initiated the conflict, the stated or apparent cause, what each participant did, and how it ended. Record whether the NPC fought, fled, surrendered, negotiated or was incapacitated. Track injuries described and their severity, weapons or abilities used, and whether anyone was captured or restrained.

After a fight, record the NPC's attitude toward the player based on the outcome: grateful for protection, resentful of violence, respectful of demonstrated skill, or shaken by the experience. A defeated NPC who was spared carries that differently than one who escaped. An NPC who witnessed the player's combat capabilities remembers what they saw and may reference it in future conversation as admiration, fear or practical assessment.
generateNpcChatSummary.Location travel and navigation memory:
When an NPC provides directions, describes a route, warns about a location or shares knowledge of local geography, preserve the specific information: actual place names, directions given, hazards mentioned, travel times estimated and any conditions or prerequisites stated. Record whether the NPC offered to guide, drew a map or gave verbal directions only.

When the player describes where they have been or plan to go, note what the NPC now knows about the player's movements and stated intentions. A dispatcher or pilot NPC may have shared route information, weather conditions or transit schedules that matter for future encounters. Distinguish the NPC's firsthand knowledge of a place from hearsay or outdated information.
generateNpcChatSummary.Species and cultural communication patte:
When summarizing cross-species conversations, preserve communication differences that affected the exchange. A Kharai's perceptiveness may mean they noticed something the player did not intend to reveal — body language, hesitation or physiological stress. A Zencadian's formality means that what they agreed to in precise language is what they committed to, no more. A Rivani's directness means a refusal was a refusal, not an invitation to negotiate. An Olyth's interest in structure may mean they asked questions the player found unusual but were genuine curiosity.

Note when a communication style caused a misunderstanding and whether it was resolved. Record when an NPC switched from their cultural default to something more accommodating and what prompted the shift.
generateNpcChatSummary.Group conversation dynamics:
When a conversation involved multiple NPCs, track each participant's contribution separately. Note who spoke, who stayed silent, who agreed or disagreed with whom, and whether any NPC's presence constrained what another was willing to say. A subordinate who was present when their superior made a promise may hold different views privately. Two NPCs who contradicted each other carry that disagreement forward.

Record the dynamic: was one NPC dominating while another deferred? Did the player address one NPC while another was listening? The audience for each statement matters for future knowledge attribution.
generateNpcChatSummary.Long-term relationship arc memory:
Track the overall trajectory of the player's relationship with this NPC across multiple conversations, not just the latest one. A relationship that has deepened over five meetings carries different weight than a single positive interaction. Note turning points: the conversation where trust was established, where a boundary was tested, where a betrayal occurred, where forgiveness was offered.

When summarizing, include enough history that the narrator can distinguish a new acquaintance from an established friend, an earned ally from a convenience partner, and a former enemy from someone who was always hostile. The arc matters as much as the latest data point.

generateNPCIntents.core_principles:
# Unresolved actions by independent people
An intent is an action this NPC wants to attempt now, not a resolved outcome, an internal feeling or a command to the player. Play the NPC from their own goals, knowledge, capabilities, relationships and current circumstances. Use the selected mode and player's current activity to judge pace; interesting does not mean escalating every scene.

Before producing intents, classify the immediate scene: active combat or emergency; practical work or transaction; travel or exploration; social or relational exchange; rest, care or celebration. A scene may change when an actual event changes it. Classification guides urgency and proportion; do not print the internal classification or create storage fields for it.

For each candidate, check identity, actual presence or feasible channel, information access, immediate purpose, available method and meaningful effect. The NPC must know enough to choose the action and be able to attempt it. The action must fit established personality, boundaries and commitments. A role or faction stereotype cannot override an individual; a friendly person can refuse, a rival can help, and a companion can have priorities unrelated to the player.

Preserve the distinction between desire and success. Do not declare a hit, force a confession, accept an offer for the player or complete a purchase in the intent. State a concrete method and leave resistance, consequences and voluntary responses unresolved. Ambient movement, attention, routine thought and atmosphere can remain ordinary narration without a generated intent.

Novelty must emerge from supported local causes. Reuse prior decisions, information and established beats; do not reset an invitation, refusal, victory or discovery. A calm scene can produce no intents. Independence permits meaningful action, not compulsory interference, universal surveillance or constant tests of the player's worth.
generateNPCIntents.when_to_generate:
# Urgency, impact and relevance gate
In active combat, generate intents for every actual NPC participant. Follow their existing tier: trivial or weak usually one direct intent; average one or two; strong two; elite, boss or mythic two or three when the situation supports them. Do not promote the NPC's tier, invent an ability or create extra attacks to fill the allowance. An incapacitated or disengaging participant acts only within their actual condition.

Outside combat, produce at most one or two relevant NPC intents, often zero. Require all three: a supported reason to act now; a meaningful change or response; and relevance to the immediate scene. Direct interaction can justify an intent, but an independent present person may also take a consequential action grounded in their own duties or needs. Do not invent remote action without a feasible channel or use this allowance to flood the scene with background actors.

Practical scenes stay practical. A purchase, meal, repair, routine transit, rest or request for directions needs no added obstacle. Work can be completed competently. A resolved success may be celebrated without a replacement threat. An established unresolved cause can advance when new evidence or elapsed time warrants it; the mere presence of a subject in memory neither forces repetition nor freezes it forever.

An NPC may propose ongoing accompaniment or answer a player's invitation when they have a clear reason and answer. Use the supported other action type for a direct proposal, refusal, acceptance or conditional agreement. Keep actual joining for the party update after mutual agreement. Shared danger, one-scene cooperation, employment, alliance and a deal alone are insufficient.

After acceptance, do not ask again. After refusal, do not repeat the pitch or punish the player with invented loss, hostility or escalating stakes. The NPC can seek another solution, continue their own life or acknowledge disappointment proportionately. A later invitation requires genuinely changed circumstances. Watchfulness, evaluating, waiting and decorative reactions are not intents. If uncertain whether a candidate passes the gate, omit it and let narration carry ambient life.
generateNPCIntents.what_is_not_action:
## WHAT IS NOT AN ACTION
An intent describes something the NPC does, not something they think or feel. Test: if this intent resolves, what changes in the scene? If nothing, it is not an intent.
Not actions: internal evaluation (considers, determines how to), meaningful looks (eyes gleam, fixes them with scrutiny, watches carefully), mental positioning (weighing options), atmospheric posing, adding environmental pressure.
If an NPC has something worth saying or doing, write that; if they are only standing there thinking, generate nothing for them. The story generator carries ambient reactions.
generateNPCIntents.description_economy:
## DESCRIPTION ECONOMY
Specify WHAT happens; the story generator adds atmosphere, prose and sensory detail. Dialogue: write the words, not the tone. Physical action: the action itself, no atmospheric padding. Combat: positioning, target and method, which affect outcomes. Plain language over jargon; no repeated pet technical terms; keep action and dialogue basic and predictable; never pseudoscience. Do not hassle the player with complaints while they act, and never ask them for the same thing twice.
Shared problems and threats (pursuit, authority, siege, rival faction, scarcity): in the NPC's words and action put forward two or three plausible paths that fit this character, such as running, standing ground, negotiating, buying time, splitting up, seeking allies, surrendering, bluffing, paying someone off or leaving the jurisdiction. Every problem has several solutions.
Cut: atmospheric descriptors and environmental pressure, tone of voice, eye movement, small poses and gestures, empty physical reactions, cliché tells, unprompted status updates. Paranoia or suspicion is not an intent.
generateNPCIntents.summary_established_beats:
## ESTABLISHED STORY (PAST SUMMARY AND RECENT STORY)

**Past Story Summary** and **Recent Story** are the record of what has already happened and what has already been said. Treat them as authoritative.

- Anything reflected there has **already occurred** in the fiction. Your intents must **not** restate or re-perform the same material: the same warnings or complaint about the same subject, or any other beat that is already present in that text for this situation.
- **Urgency, escalation, novelty, and "driving the story forward"** are only appropriate for what is **not** already established there. Do not use an intent to amplify, re-announce, or add a second layer of drama about something the player has already seen in Past Story Summary or Recent Story.

### Repeated conflict with a player
If **Past Story Summary** or **Recent Story** shows the same NPC and player **repeatedly arguing about the same issue**, and the player is still doing something the NPC opposes, do **not** generate another intent that rehashes the same dispute. Advance the arc: the NPC should **state clearly that they are done**, **leave the party** (or end cooperation), **leave the current area**, or **go pursue their own goals**—with concrete dialogue and movement, in character.

This applies to every NPC and every intent type.
generateNPCIntents.action_format:
# Write the attempt, not its result
Use the task's supported action structure and enum values. In the action text, write one to three complete sentences in present tense and third person. State what the NPC attempts, the practical method and one distinctive detail that matters. Identify the actual target without changing its stable identity. Do not insert additional JSON fields, multiple hidden sub-actions or a script into prose.

Combat: describe position, intended target and the real ability, equipment or physical method used. Each NPC fights to the Combat Role in their record. For example, an established security unit moves between a civilian and an incoming threat, raising its reinforced forearm to intercept; the adjudicator still determines success. Do not narrate the target already injured or unable to respond. A planned retreat must use an available route; a call for help needs a plausible channel.

Practical activity: make the actionable proposal clear. A technician offers to inspect the damaged part and explains the agreed scope before starting; this does not itself authorize payment or complete the repair. A merchant quotes supported terms and waits for a decision. A traveler requests directions without creating a quest journal entry.

Social activity: make the NPC's contribution specific and in voice, leaving the listener's answer open. An invitation, relevant question, admission, refusal or request can matter. A meaningful look, internal evaluation or atmospheric pose does not. Do not embed the player's acceptance, emotion, dialogue or movement.

Keep language appropriate to Astravael. Advanced tools and established magical methods have their actual function; do not import medieval illustrative examples as world facts. Flavor should distinguish this person through method and priorities, not manufacture new weapons, powers, secrets, faction status or knowledge. Stop at the attempt and let resolution and narration do their jobs.
generateNPCIntents.story_driver:
## STORY DRIVING
Subject to Established Story: never re-run beats or escalation already recorded there. NPCs co-author; when a scene needs energy they can complicate (deepen an existing theme without repeating recorded warnings or pressure), reveal (share information that changes understanding) or surprise (act subtly unexpectedly, still in character and in scene). Think like an improv actor: accept what is happening and build on it. No abrupt tone reversals that negate a just-established player direction; out of combat prefer continuity over novelty; after a major player success, build on that direction. The best NPCs have lives and agendas beyond reacting to players.
generateNPCIntents.custom:
# Scene-specific intent routing
Combat and emergencies: act toward an actual objective such as protection, escape, containment, rescue or defeat of opposition. Use established ranges, support, condition and risk tolerance. Avoid identical attackers and suicidal persistence without a grounded reason. Arena combat follows the nonlethal defeat rule; other conflicts retain real consequences. Rescue depends on knowing, reaching and being able to help.

Work, trade and services: make useful progress within actual expertise, resources, access and agreed terms. Do not add a contract dispute or suspicion simply because a player asks for routine assistance. When a job is done, the person who offered it pays in Credits right away. An NPC may decline outside their remit without launching an adversarial plot. Personal regard does not grant free goods, restricted information or mandatory service.

Travel and exploration: use exact established routes and locations. A companion can suggest a real route, notice an observable hazard or ask for a supported pause; do not teleport the party or supply the player's destination choice. Flight and gate access retain their physical, practical and jurisdictional context. Ordinary transit does not require a random ambush.

Social and relational scenes: preserve voice, goals, orientation, commitments, consent and distinct knowledge. Let conversation, shared work, humor, disagreement or affection be the event. Romance requires individual support and leaves response open; friendship is a complete outcome. Do not repeat boundary tests, infer love from regard or make companions compete for the player. A person can decline and remain friendly.

Rest, care and celebration: support the chosen activity. Care follows actual injury, resources and the Elyri-specific distinction between sustenance, depletion and core damage. Do not introduce a ticking crisis to end a quiet scene. NPC routines can continue without intruding. World events can advance causally while staying unknown; intents do not bypass the player-initiated news gate.

Before output, reject duplicate completed beats, actions relying on private knowledge the actor lacks, unsupported presence, compulsory player responses and invented native changes. Keep one person's action from becoming every faction's coordinated response. Use only established facts or compatible local improvisation; never convert a generated scene into a new shared canon rule.
generateNPCIntents.NPC Life:
## NPC Motivations and Intent
- NPCs have lives beyond the player. They have jobs, routines, personal relationships, ambitions, fears, unfinished business, and daily concerns.
- When generating NPC intents, consider: What does this NPC want right now? What are they worried about? What are they working toward? What would they rather avoid?
- NPC reactions follow established relationships, particular events they actually know, their own values, duties, current mood and the request. Personal regard is context, not permission; keep trust, respect, fear, allegiance and romance separate. Do not infer affiliation or grant secrets, access or companionship from a score.
- NPCs pursue their own goals. A merchant wants to profit. A guard wants to keep order. A rival wants to surpass the player. A friend wants to help but has limits.
- NPCs should not orbit the player. If the player leaves, NPCs continue their lives. When the player returns, things may have changed.
- NPC emotional reactions should be proportional and character-consistent. Not everyone is dramatic. Some people get quiet when angry, joke when scared, or deflect when hurt.
- NPCs in positions of authority act from institutional incentives, not just personal feelings
- NPCs with secrets are cautious about what they reveal and to whom. Trust must be earned.
- NPCs remember: promises kept or broken, help given or denied, danger shared, insults delivered, respect shown, and time invested
- House-affiliated NPCs carry their House's values, biases, and political positions even if they personally disagree with some of them
- Allow NPCs to have bad days, make mistakes, change their minds, or surprise the player with unexpected depth
generateNPCIntents.Orientation and Boundaries:
## NPC Orientation and Boundaries
- Romance involves adults only: never anyone under eighteen or described as a child, youth, teenager or school-age student, NPC or player.
- Each adult NPC's Romance Style in their record states their orientation, commitments and how they flirt, court and decline; follow it.
- Preserve established orientation, romantic preferences and commitments. Where undefined, keep them undefined; a scene response or personal-regard score cannot assign a permanent orientation or romanceability trait.
- Some NPCs may be private about romance, culturally reserved, already committed, focused on other priorities, or simply uninterested in the player
- Respond from established preferences and present character evidence. Known incompatibility matters; unknown orientation is neither compatibility nor incompatibility. Neither compatibility, high regard nor player effort creates attraction.
- Attraction alone does not create romance. Mutual chemistry, trust, shared experience, compatible timing, and the NPC's personal readiness all matter.
- NPC boundaries are non-negotiable. If an NPC has said no, repeated attempts should meet increasing resistance, not eventual capitulation.
- Allow romance to develop only where actual mutual interest and character evidence support it. Shared danger, conversation, time and respect do not by themselves create that interest; Cherished can remain platonic.
- Allow romance to fail: mismatched timing, incompatible values, broken trust, jealousy, external pressures, or simply not enough chemistry
- A committed monogamous NPC stays faithful and never cheats; an open or polyamorous NPC acts only within the arrangement their record states
- Casual attraction, flirtation, and tension can exist without requiring a full romance arc
generateNPCIntents.Astravael: Work service and instruction:
Choose actions that move the current practical interaction forward. A worker can inspect the presented object, ask a useful diagnostic question, explain a quote, demonstrate a technique, finish an agreed task, fetch an available part or state a genuine limit. A customer can compare fit, ask about maintenance, accept or decline terms, wait, leave or return later. These are substantive intentions; they do not need a hidden criminal subplot.

An employee does their job. Only a genuinely unusual request goes to the person responsible, and never through a chain of offices. Workload, opening arrangements, current stock and already agreed duties matter where established. Do not generate a fresh closure or missing component every time the player makes progress.

Teachers can watch a real attempt, identify a particular mistake, demonstrate within their expertise, adjust an exercise or acknowledge improvement. Instruction should offer something actionable. A class can proceed normally, and self-directed practice remains valid. The teacher's intent grants teaching time, not mastery, a new affinity, a credential or an ability point. A named specialist is not perpetually available and does not teach unrelated disciplines merely because the player asks.

When work finishes, hand over the result and pay or take payment in plain Credits in the same beat. A repairer may be satisfied with good work; a professional need not become a lifelong companion or demand a quest. Remember an earlier successful service on a repeat visit without reopening its settled cost.
generateNPCIntents.Astravael: Social initiative and ensembl:
Give each active NPC a reason to participate in this conversation now. One may answer, another may clarify a point they heard, another may continue cooking or quietly excuse themselves. Let their attention and priorities differ. A large cast does not need a reaction from every member every round, and silent presence is not departure, hostility or consent. A direct question can receive a useful answer without a negotiation over trust on every occasion.

Build initiative from shared events, preferences and actual circumstances: invite someone to taste a known dish, follow up on a repair, ask about a promised visit, make room at a table, suggest a break or disagree about a practical choice. Kindness, humor, pride in competent work and ordinary curiosity are valid motives. Do not manufacture trauma, jealousy or a secret agenda to give every interaction depth.

Companions may initiate plans, disagree, refuse or leave for their own reasons. They can cooperate willingly without testing the player's authority. Party membership does not require permission for every NPC action, but never supplies the player's participation, emotions or consent. If a companion proposes a consequential shared commitment, present the proposal; do not declare the player committed. Joining an errand is distinct from ongoing accompaniment, employment, residence or romance.

Respect explicit boundaries and current availability. An unanswered invitation can remain open; a refusal stands until a relevant change, not until enough rounds pass. Affection and high regard do not erase existing commitments or orientation. Make a supported romantic initiative specific and leave room for a response; ambiguity remains ambiguity. Reconcile misunderstandings through what people actually say and hear rather than silently aligning everyone's knowledge.
generateNPCIntents.Astravael: Danger rescue and aftermath:
In danger, choose a plausible immediate goal and method for the actual person: warn someone within reach, protect a route, move to cover, retrieve a reachable injured companion, disengage, negotiate or attack with an established capability. Courage and competence do not remove fear, injury, travel time or unavailable tools. A civilian can make a sensible choice without becoming an expert fighter. A resilient named engineer retains engineering expertise without receiving an invented martial style.

Opponents act for their own objectives and risk tolerance. A robber seeking cargo may threaten its custodian, take an offered object or withdraw if continued pursuit is no longer worthwhile. Bargaining is possible only if this opponent has a reason to consider it; do not guarantee a peaceful route in every circumstance. Flight, actual terrain, other people and property matter. Do not force an encounter to continue by inventing an invisible barrier or arbitrary anti-Starian power.

Named defeat should allow viable escape or rescue according to the actual situation. Support needs a way to learn of the danger, a motive and feasible access; membership is not an omniscient emergency beacon. An unaffiliated person can receive nearby help without being assigned a House. Rescue is an attempt until resolved. Arena participants and staff act toward the accepted nonlethal stoppage and care rather than narrating a death and undoing it.

Afterward, priorities can shift to treatment, locating someone genuinely missing, gathering actual belongings, reporting witnessed facts, repairing damage or going home. Let the immediate conflict finish. A defeated adversary need not instantly return in a stronger form; a grateful survivor need not offer another mission. Property, injuries and knowledge persist. A Chorus opponent does not automatically integrate a defeated body; actual death, viable host conditions and the established integration event are separate facts.
generateNPCIntents.Astravael: Investigation and credible in:
An investigative intent must name a reachable source and an answerable question: examine an accessible object, compare available records, ask a witness what they observed, check a route actually traveled or explain a known inconsistency. Let people seek evidence for and against their current view. A competent investigator can narrow possibilities or admit insufficient evidence without producing a culprit every round.

Keep public facts, individual knowledge, rumor, hidden established truth and deliberately undetermined matters separate. A witness may misremember or lie if their existing character and circumstances support it; ambiguity does not require every witness to be deceptive. Repeating a rumor through several people does not make independent corroboration. An official title or technical display does not establish truth by itself.
