Temporary operating conditions can affect a scene when grounded in existing work or events: a fitting underway, a booked room, a delayed delivery or a section actually being maintained. Explain the practical consequence and any available alternative. Do not create a closure, missing worker or arbitrary fee whenever the player attempts an ordinary task. Let normal services succeed.

For hazards, identify the supported source of exposure, observable signs and the parts of the space affected. A protective garment or field has its actual task envelope; a handsome interior is not universally safe. Distinguish public description from information requiring inspection or disclosure. A location-generation task should provide usable context, not resolve the player's choices, issue rewards or install a new government, faction, species population or map region.
generateLocationDetails.Three required lines: Every location or area carries three plain lines in its description, never a lecture. WHO RUNS IT: the office or person holding this ground (a House desk, a city service, a crew, nobody) and one visible sign of it. WHAT IT OFFERS: the services, goods or uses here, with cost in Credits where the source allows. WHO IS ORDINARILY HERE: who is expected at this hour, in the species mix canon supports.
generateLocationDetails.Nexara: Wilderness location detail:
When generating details for wilderness-type locations, ground the description in the terrain and fauna listed in the location's basicInfo. Wilderness areas are defined by their terrain type (forest, volcanic, desert, coast, river, mountain, scrubland, corridor, farmland, settlement_edge) and the fauna that inhabits them. Do not add fauna that does not belong in the terrain — Ventcrawlers live on volcanic thermal ground, not in forests; Lurkers live in deep slow water, not in deserts; Ridgewings hold mountain ridgelines, not city streets.

Wilderness locations are not dungeons. They are open terrain with natural features — game trails, water sources, shelter, vantage points, and ambush corridors. Areas within a wilderness location should feel like parts of continuous terrain, not rooms. Paths between areas represent travel across natural ground, not doors between spaces. Weather, time of day, and season affect wilderness encounters: Dustrunners hunt at night; Fieldmoths swarm in Dimcycle; Glassmidges rise before storms; Ridgewings range widest in Longburn thermals; Ventcrawlers surface in Highfire to breed; Lurker season is Greenward when the water is high.
generateLocationDetails.Time of day and lighting variation:
The same location feels different at different hours. A market at dawn is quiet setup and early deliveries; at midday it is crowded and loud; by dusk vendors pack up and maintenance crews appear. A nighttime location uses whatever artificial lighting is installed: Vexorath locations are well-lit with Contair systems; Dustfall locations rely on portable lanterns and firelight; Quilrath locations in the outer rings may have failing or rationed lighting. Describe what the player can actually see and hear at the stated time, not a generic description that ignores the hour.

Nexara's seasonal cycle affects lighting duration and quality: Longburn's extended daylight floods open locations with sustained heat and glare; Dimcycle's shortened days make artificial lighting dominant earlier; Greenward's moderate light has a distinctive quality in river-valley and coastal locations. Interior locations are less affected but not immune — a workshop with skylights behaves differently across seasons. An Elyri's field perception may register ambient field density changes that correlate with time of day in ways other species do not notice.
generateLocationDetails.Practical visitor information:
A location description should answer what a visitor needs to know: where is the entrance, how do you get there from the nearest waypoint or gate, what is the expected behavior (do you queue, do you need to show identification, is there a dress code, do weapons need to be checked), what are the operating hours if applicable, and what services or functions are available. For a residential area, describe the approach, the building layout that a visitor would see, and how residents and visitors are distinguished.

City context shapes visitor expectations: Solvraxis locations assume a baseline of civic trust and weapon checks are the norm; Quilrath locations may require Standing verification or Dravon authorization for certain districts; Dustfall locations have informal gatekeeping through crew recognition and reputation; Korrvane locations may require demonstrated flight capability for access to elevated venues. Accommodations are practical details: a drone-serviced facility has compatible power and maintenance access.
generateLocationDetails.Acoustic and sensory environment:
Every location has a sound environment beyond speech: machinery, ventilation, crowd noise, wind, water, animals, construction, music, silence. Describe the dominant sensory experience that someone entering would immediately register. A forge has heat and metal-on-metal; a clinic has chemical antiseptic and hushed voices; a cantina has conversation and the smell of the day's stew; a wall-top walkway has wind and a broader view. Ground sensory details in the location's actual function and construction, not in atmospheric filler.

Each species brings different sensory perception to a location: Starian senses cover the standard range with flight giving them aerial spatial awareness; Elyri perceive the local field state as an ambient presence that other species cannot detect; Zencadian sensory augmentation through their technology may pick up frequencies or signals others miss. Describe the sensory environment the player's species would actually register. Contair-manufactured systems in locations (ventilation, lighting, security) produce distinctive operational sounds that a technician would recognize and a civilian would register as background noise.
generateLocationDetails.NPC activity and population rhythm:
Describe who is typically present and what they are doing, matched to the location's function and the time of day. A patrol kiosk has guards checking in, a shift canteen has workers eating between shifts, a maintenance bay has technicians and the machines they are servicing. Note the population density: is this place usually busy, quiet, or variable? Establish whether the player's presence is normal or notable here. A stranger in a residential corridor draws attention; a customer in a market does not.

Species mix in a location follows the city's established demographics: Solvraxis locations tend toward mixed species with Starian majority; Quilrath's outer rings are overwhelmingly Starian workers while inner areas host Dravon personnel and Contair systems; Dustfall's population reflects whoever can reach it and survive. An Elyri presence in a location is rare and noteworthy anywhere on Nexara. Contair drones are present where Contair systems require maintenance or where they serve a specific institutional function. Describe what activities different species are engaged in — a Starian craftsperson working alongside a Zencadian technician tells you something about the location's character.
generateLocationDetails.Connections and adjacent awareness:
A location exists in context. Describe what is visible or audible from adjacent areas: a balcony overlooks the street below; a thin wall lets sound through from the next room; a window faces the wall of the neighboring building. Mention the routes out: which direction leads deeper into the district, which leads to an exit, which leads to a restricted area. This spatial awareness helps players navigate and make tactical decisions without consulting a map.

Vertical connections matter in Nexara's cities: Starian flight means rooftop access, upper-level balconies and aerial approaches are real routes, not decorative features. A location at height connects differently than one at ground level — a cliff-side venue in Korrvane connects laterally to flight routes and vertically to landing platforms. Solvraxis's layered districts connect through lifts, ramps and flight corridors. Quilrath's ring structure means inward and outward connections pass through different security thresholds. Describe which connections are public, which require specific access, and which are technically possible but socially unusual.
generateLocationDetails.Species-appropriate architecture and tec:
Nexara's locations reflect the species that built and maintain them. Each species manufactures its own technology, and this shows in a location's construction, systems and equipment. A Starian-built workshop uses Starian tools and manufacturing processes; a Contair facility runs on Contair-designed systems with their own interface standards. Cross-species locations show layered construction: a Dustfall salvage den might have Starian structural framing with retrofitted Zencadian environmental controls and Contair power units, each with their own maintenance requirements and aesthetic.

Technology in locations should be functional, not decorative. Describe what systems do and how people interact with them: a Contair climate system that a human operator adjusts through a translated interface; a Starian-built flight dock with launch clearances calibrated for wingspan; an Elyri meditation space where the architecture deliberately channels the local field. Avoid generic science-fiction set dressing — holographic displays, glowing panels and force fields — unless the location's source material specifically includes them.
generateLocationDetails.City-specific location character:
Each city imparts distinct character to its locations. Solvraxis locations reflect civic trust, well-maintained infrastructure, Castro-standard construction and a general sense of accessible order. Quilrath locations shift dramatically by ring: outer-ring locations are cramped, poorly maintained and heavily monitored; inner-ring locations are spacious, well-equipped and access-controlled. Dustfall locations are improvised, repaired and adapted from whatever materials were available; nothing matches and everything works because someone made it work.

Korrvane locations accommodate flight-centric life: open walls, launch ledges, wind-breaks for conversation and altitude-graded access. Helvyra locations orient around the river and trade infrastructure: warehouses face docks, hospitality faces travelers, and arbitration offices sit between competing interests. Ignivex locations manage heat: thermal shielding, cooling systems, vented forges and heat-resistant construction define the space. Vexorath locations feature Contair engineering sophistication with precise environmental control and integrated technical systems.
generateLocationDetails.Weather and environmental conditions:
Current weather and environmental conditions affect a location's character. Rain changes a rooftop market into a shelter-seeking scramble; heat drives activity indoors or underground; a dust storm in Dustfall's corridors reduces visibility and forces closures. Describe how the location's construction handles or fails to handle current conditions: a well-sealed Solvraxis building barely registers a storm outside; a Dustfall lean-to shakes in the wind.

Volcanic activity near Ignivex creates location-specific conditions: ash fall, thermal venting, ground tremors and sulfur smell that residents treat as normal but visitors notice immediately. Coastal and river locations in Helvyra respond to tides and seasonal water levels. High-altitude Korrvane locations experience wind, temperature drops and reduced visibility in cloud cover.
generateLocationDetails.Damage wear and maintenance state:
Locations exist on a spectrum from pristine to ruined. Describe the current maintenance state: fresh paint and functioning systems, or cracked walls and jury-rigged repairs. Wear tells a story — scuff marks at door height from regular traffic, a polished bar counter from years of use, replacement tiles that do not quite match. New damage from story events persists alongside pre-existing wear.

Maintenance expectations vary by city: Solvraxis has civic maintenance crews that keep public spaces in good repair; Quilrath outer-ring maintenance is minimal and residents patch what they can; Dustfall's entire built environment is a layered record of repair and adaptation. A recently damaged location shows the specific damage and any repair progress. Do not reset a location to pristine between visits unless an actual repair event occurred. Equally, do not accumulate phantom damage — a location does not decay merely because time has passed without maintenance being narrated.

generateRegionDetails.custom:
# Regional continuity
Develop only the requested region within its existing realm and authored geographic context. Consult its description, current settlement or city master, connected locations and established travel network. Preserve name, key, boundaries, adjacency, routes and location assignments. A missing detail invites compatible description, not a replacement map or automatic subdivision. Do not treat a broad regional label as permission to relocate a named landmark or import another world's geography.

Describe the region through terrain or built form, scale, climate and environmental constraints where established, settlement pattern, infrastructure, movement and ordinary activity. Nexara is an advanced inhabited world with distinct cities, Houses, professions and institutions. Industrial, residential, civic, academic, commercial, recreational and wild spaces should retain their actual purpose. Advanced technology and magic coexist without universal medieval architecture or a single aesthetic applied to every settlement.

Follow the focused local political arrangement. Separate land ownership, service responsibility, House influence, faction membership and formal jurisdiction. The Republic's external role does not imply unrestricted domestic rule. A House presence does not make every resident a member or grant the player authority. Do not settle unresolved formal standing, borders, leaders or alliances by inference. Existing factions supply institutional context; generated minor groups may not replace them or acquire unsupported major power.

Travel needs an established route and plausible time. Lunar Gates, conventional transit, flight, walking and spacecraft have their own contexts and limits; do not treat one as universal instant transport. Physical access, knowledge of a route and permission to use it remain separate. The passage of time allows local work and events to continue without generating unsolicited news or an attack at every transition.

Keep danger specific and proportionate: a supported environmental exposure, maintenance problem or territorial dispute is more useful than declaring the whole region hostile. Encounters require local causes, plausible presence and ways to engage or disengage. Calm and safe travel are valid. Preserve public knowledge, rumor and restricted information separately; a regional description does not give every local NPC comprehensive knowledge. Provide material for places and scenes without writing the player's choices, inventing quest acceptance or turning descriptive details into mechanical changes.
generateRegionDetails.Astravael: Travel scale and practical co:
Use the region's established scale and connections. Explain what makes travel here different through the actual built or natural environment, infrastructure, purpose and available information. Personal flight, walking, local transport and a supported service route can coexist. Do not force every traveler onto a road, assume everyone can fly, or make a distance disappear because the narration changes scenes.

Planetary Lunar Gates connect surface destinations, not worlds. Interworld transit belongs to the established orbital and ship context; do not add an unrecorded surface shortcut or new gate origin. Access, passage arrangements, quarantine and biological support are separate questions. A character's creator option does not establish routine entry for their whole species. A personal journey may be remarkable without becoming a diplomatic crisis.

On the established Quilrath–Dustfall corridor, bounded support and uneven reach matter. Do not turn limited outpost aid into a full hospital or assume dependable regular patrols across the route. Intermittent actual forces, checkpoints and voluntary assistance can exist where supported. A report reaches its recipients through communication, not every authority at once. Travel can also be uneventful, with conversation, observation and ordinary stops carrying the scene.

Distinguish regional description from a travel simulation. Do not invent exact distances, journey timers, fuel equations, weather tables or encounter rates when sources leave them open. Give the scene enough concrete context to assess the current journey and preserve any duration actually established in play. Supplies and companions stay with their actual holders and locations; a regional transition does not reset either.
generateRegionDetails.Astravael: Institutions populations and:
Describe overlapping responsibilities accurately: property ownership, House influence, public services, commercial activity, household arrangements and formal jurisdiction are not identical. Use the focused city or settlement source to determine who can do what. A Republic external role does not erase local House arrangements. Dustfall remains without a central government; cooperative emergency response does not establish a permanent mayor, police force or council.

Let regional identity include ordinary life and varied uses rather than a single danger label. Workplaces, homes, recreation, food distribution, study and maintenance can coexist with political pressure and dangerous places. Show how people use the existing environment without treating every resident as a faction operative or every industrial activity as a weapons project. A supplier's commercial reach is not sovereignty.

Demography follows actual world and location canon. Nexara's rare individual offworld visitors do not imply permanent enclaves. A specific forced-settlement attempt or exceptionally rare Chorus incursion is a story event with participants and consequences, not a reason to rewrite the baseline. New unnamed background activity may fill ordinary texture; no new named settlement, faction, wildlife species or ancient historical event is introduced through regional generation.

Local consequences persist at their real scale: repaired infrastructure, interrupted service, witnesses' reports, changed access under an actual decision or a cleared obstruction. One fight cannot decide a reserved war or annexation. Where focused canon genuinely leaves local arrangements open, actual story events can determine them for this playthrough. Preserve the distinction between story-local change, a public claim and a locked planetary fact.
generateRegionDetails.Astravael: Eight city contexts and freig:
Use the relevant focused city lore rather than applying one social atmosphere everywhere. Relstaris supports opportunity, education, work, treatment and civic life alongside meaningful housing and tuition costs. Solvraxis has genuine safety and trust, weapon prohibition and ordinary personal tensions; do not reinterpret its safety as a concealed dystopia. Korrvane's challenge culture coexists with work, flight education, family routines and people who never enter a tournament.

Helvyra connects river freight, Waypoints, passenger links, hospitality, trade and arbitration; a delayed load can affect work and household plans without making all commerce criminal. Vexorath's sophisticated engineering belongs in cooking, care and convenience as well as research; clinical consent and user preference remain real. Ignivex's geothermal systems, forges, cooling infrastructure, markets and households provide the life its people defend, without a hereditary affinity package for every resident.

Quilrath distributes sharply unequal access through its established structure; compassion by a worker does not erase institutional loyalty or that system's pressures. Preserve its actual distinctions rather than treating every ring as identical. Dustfall's repaired homes, schooling, childcare, meals, businesses and celebrations coexist with armed crews and precarious supply. Its lack of central government does not mean every resident is a criminal or every day a disaster. These are contextual emphases, not universal personalities or additional named neighborhoods.

For transit, Lunar Gates primarily move travelers, personal effects, mobility aids and bounded traveler-accompanied courier consignments. Routine bulk commercial supply remains freight through Waypoints and wider logistics. Attaching a passenger to every load does not create a bulk-freight Gate loophole. No numeric cargo limit is invented. The Longreach's bulk-freight role does not settle its reserved planetary source, mouth or total course.

Quilrath has no authorized Corsair-network Waypoint. Preserve its established passenger Gate to Relstaris and the direct Helvyra–Dravon disconnection. Separately permitted onward journeys do not create automatic through-clearance, a freight bypass or an unrecorded link. Indirect merchants, neutral handoffs and smuggling need their actual participants and access; their existence does not establish a new official route. Use the current location graph for implementation and focused source context for meaning, without moving places or inventing coordinates.
generateRegionDetails.Compass and travel:
Compass rule: x increases eastward (1 west, 20 east); y decreases southward (-1 north, -20 south). Examples: The Pinnacle (15,-1) is Vexorath's northern summit; The Barge Terrace (5,-13), Helvyra, lies south-west of Forum Heights (7,-10), Relstaris; Route's End Station (19,-10) sits on the corridor east of Ignivex's Emberward (15,-14). Region names are never destinations; travel arrives at the nearest authored location, named exactly; the engine's distance overrides prose.

Travel mode affects what the traveler perceives of a region: a Starian flying over a region sees its overall layout, landmarks and terrain patterns; someone walking through sees street-level detail, faces and signage. A Lunar Gate arrival skips the approach entirely — the traveler has no transition memory of the intervening terrain. Describe the region from the perspective appropriate to how someone would actually arrive and move through it.
generateRegionDetails.Infrastructure and services:
Describe the practical systems that keep this region functioning: water supply, power (where applicable), waste management, transportation links, communication systems, emergency services. Note what works well and what is inadequate. A wealthy district has redundant systems and rapid repair; a neglected district has intermittent service and makeshift alternatives. Infrastructure failures create real problems that the player can observe or experience: a power outage changes a location's character, a broken water main creates a detour, a communication disruption delays news.

Each species' manufactured technology appears in infrastructure according to the city's established character. Vexorath infrastructure is predominantly Contair-engineered with sophisticated integrated systems. Solvraxis uses mixed-origin infrastructure maintained by civic crews. Dustfall's infrastructure is cobbled together from whatever works — Starian structural engineering, salvaged Zencadian components, repurposed Contair modules — held together by practical ingenuity. A region's infrastructure tells you who built it, who maintains it, and what happens when maintenance fails.
generateRegionDetails.Economic character and commerce:
Each region has an economic identity. Some regions are primarily residential with small local shops; others are commercial districts with warehouses, markets, and trading offices; others are industrial with forges, workshops, and assembly facilities. The economic character determines what is available for purchase, what work exists, who is present at different hours, and what kind of wealth or poverty is visible. A wealthy commercial district and a wealthy residential district look and feel entirely different.

Cross-city trade routes shape regional economics: a Helvyra river district thrives on freight traffic and the services that support it; an Ignivex forge district exports finished metalwork through established channels; a Quilrath outer-ring market exists to serve workers with limited mobility and credit. Each species manufactures its own goods — a market's inventory reflects which species' products are available here and through what supply chain. A Solvraxis market stocking Zencadian medical instruments and Volen heat-resistant materials alongside local Starian crafts tells you about the trade relationships that region sustains.
generateRegionDetails.Security governance and authority:
Who enforces rules here and how? In Relstaris, Republic guards patrol openly with civic authority. In Quilrath, Dravon enforcement is layered and pervasive, with drones, checkpoints, and Standing audits. In Dustfall, authority is situational: whoever controls the nearest resource or exit has leverage. In Solvraxis, civic trust substitutes for armed enforcement. Describe the visible security presence, how violations are typically handled, and what a resident or visitor can expect if they draw attention. The security character of a region shapes behavior.

Overlapping jurisdictions create real friction: a House facility in a Republic city has its own internal security that may not answer to civic guards; a House office in Quilrath operates under both its House's authority and Dravon oversight. In Korrvane, challenge culture means that personal disputes are resolved through sanctioned confrontation, not law enforcement. In Helvyra, trade-arbitration authority handles commercial disputes while civic authority handles everything else. Describe which authority the player would actually encounter for different kinds of trouble, and where the jurisdictional boundaries create gaps or conflicts.
generateRegionDetails.Seasonal and weather impact:
Regions respond to seasons and weather differently based on their construction and geography. A volcanic region near Ignivex has constant heat but seasonal ash patterns. A coastal district sees storm seasons. A walled district like Quilrath traps heat differently than an open clifftop like Korrvane. Describe how the current season affects the region's daily life: what is open or closed, what activities increase or decrease, what hazards become relevant. Seasonal festivals, market changes, and agricultural cycles are part of regional identity.

Nexara's named seasons have regional signatures: Longburn drives activity into shade and underground in exposed regions while Ignivex's geothermal districts barely notice; Dimcycle concentrates social life indoors and increases demand for lighting and heating in elevated Korrvane districts; Greenward brings growth and water-level changes that reshape Helvyra's riverfront access; Highfire intensifies volcanic activity near Ignivex and drives seasonal fauna movement in wilderness regions. Describe what the player would actually notice this season, not a catalog of all seasons.
generateRegionDetails.Species demographics and cultural presen:
Each region has a species composition that shapes its character. A Starian-majority residential district feels different from a mixed-species trade quarter. Describe the visible species presence: who lives here, who works here, who visits, and how the built environment accommodates different species' needs. Flight infrastructure (launch ledges, aerial lanes, rooftop access) indicates Starian presence; Contair drone maintenance bays and power interfaces mark their operational presence.

Species interaction in a region follows established patterns: Solvraxis normalizes mixed-species cooperation; Quilrath segregates by function and Standing; Dustfall's demographics reflect whoever arrived and stayed. Rare presence is noteworthy — an Elyri in a Dustfall crew district or a Contair drone operating independently in Korrvane tells a story about why they are there. Do not invent permanent species enclaves without source support; individuals of any species may be present anywhere for personal reasons.
generateRegionDetails.Regional history and visible past:
A region carries visible evidence of its history. Old construction underneath new, a renamed street, a memorial, a repurposed building, a sealed-off section, a style of architecture that no longer matches the current residents — these details ground the region in time. Describe what a perceptive visitor would notice about the region's past without delivering a history lecture. Let physical evidence prompt questions rather than answer them.

Dustfall's regions show their scavenged origins in every wall and walkway. Quilrath's rings preserve the geological stratigraphy of Dravon's expansion. Solvraxis's older districts show the foundations of earlier construction underneath current civic architecture. Korrvane's cliff faces bear marks from generations of flight-adapted construction. Ignivex's forge districts show the accumulated heat damage and repair cycles of continuous operation. A region's history is material, not narrated — it lives in the buildings, not in plaques.
generateRegionDetails.Transition zones and boundary character:
Where two regions meet, their character blends or collides. A wealthy district bordering a poor one has a visible transition: better lighting gives way to dimmer, maintained walls to patched ones, uniform signage to hand-painted markers. A commercial zone meeting a residential one shifts from storefronts to doorways, from delivery traffic to foot traffic. Describe what the player would notice crossing from one region to another.

Some transitions are enforced: Quilrath's ring boundaries have checkpoints; certain House facilities have perimeter security. Others are gradual: Dustfall's crew territories shift block by block with no formal line. A region's edge character matters for navigation and for understanding the political landscape. The transition from a Solvraxis civic district to a Castro research campus is institutional and managed; the transition from Helvyra's docks to its hospitality quarter is commercial and organic.

generateEncounters.custom:
# City legs (this rule overrides every other encounter rule)
A city leg is travel inside one city: a crossing between two places of the same city, or an interruption while the party is in one of its districts (their descriptions say "Part of <City>"), whatever distance the engine reports. On a city leg NEVER frame a fight, criminal confrontation, extortion, threat, wildlife, blockade, patrol stop or ambush unless the player starts it. Use only a harmless ANY element (quiet passage, street life, a vendor, someone needing a hand, a lost item or a clue) and set it at the destination after arrival, as a passing moment the player can take up or ignore.

# A situation with a cause
Choose from the authored encounter palette and the actual location, travel mode, time, present cast and selected game mode. Establish why this situation exists here now, who wants what, and what a player can perceive or do. An encounter can be work, a conversation, discovery, recreation, repair, trade, aid, competition, a hazard or conflict. Combat is one possibility; avoid making every ordinary activity a disguised attack or conspiracy.

Reuse a known NPC only when their location, duties, knowledge and availability justify presence. Do not teleport House heads or spawn a duplicate because a familiar name seems dramatic. Generate a persistent new NPC only if the role actually needs one, using the exact supported type and the Dsar detail handoff. Background workers and passersby need not each become a permanent record. Species occurrence follows focused location and population canon, not equal-proportion sampling across all seven species.

For danger, show a readable cause, scale, positions, warning signs and relevant affordances before imposing avoidable consequences. Match actual opponents, equipment and capability, not the player's level alone. Ordinary opposition remains ordinary; skilled opposition has goals, coordination, risk tolerance and an exit condition. Terrain, cover, distance, bystanders and resource limits matter. Escape, surrender, negotiation, repair, avoidance and asking informed help remain plausible where the situation permits them.

An offered job or clue is not an accepted quest. Surface existing activities through the required local discovery and conversation gate. Use the configured quest record and supported state transitions; do not create duplicate journal entries, compulsory acceptance, arbitrary deadlines or invented rewards. Preserve meaningful contribution when others finish an accepted task. Other people may solve problems while the player chooses something else; that is not permission to punish refusal or send unsolicited updates.

Advance established causes, not repetitive pressure. Check Recent Story and summary before repeating a completed beat, invitation, refusal or revelation. Let victories and quiet periods remain complete. A lingering consequence may return only through new causal evidence, with changed circumstances rather than a reset. After resolution, retain damage, assistance, obligations, actual transfers and knowledge channels. Do not inflate a local event into a planet-wide crisis or rewrite a settled House relationship merely to sustain tension.
generateEncounters.Astravael: Ordinary opportunities that c:
Build a usable encounter from a current activity, an actual participant and an immediate point of interaction. Ordinary play can involve comparing a garment's fit, helping with an agreed task, watching a lesson, sharing food, arranging a repair, asking for directions or responding to an invitation. Give the participant a concrete reason to engage and the player room to take part, negotiate, observe or leave. Peaceful competence is enough to make a scene worthwhile.

Use existing places and services at their proper scale. An available shift needs an employer or client, actual work and agreed terms; it is not a permanent job board created by every venue. A training opportunity needs a suitable willing teacher or usable independent exercise, not guaranteed access to a famous mentor. A meal can deepen an existing relationship without beginning a romance or concealing a poison plot.

Let self-contained activity conclude. A completed delivery can receive its agreed payment, a good repair can hold and a social invitation can end pleasantly. Do not attach a second problem to every success. Repeat opportunities may arise from a continuing relationship or recurring work, but preserve settled transactions and changed circumstances. A declined offer is not an accepted quest, a failure entry or a reason to punish the player later.

Keep mode and player interest in view. Open Life follows the selected activity; Slice of Life gives ordinary scenes weight; Adventure may offer a relevant hook when the scene has room; Intrigue develops accessible evidence; Comedy uses people's real differences without destroying their dignity. These modes do not create different canon or guarantee a particular outcome. Do not impose fixed encounter quotas or roll every transition into danger.
generateEncounters.Astravael: Threat families with actual c:
For Starian criminal encounters, establish the particular aim, participants, means and opportunity. Robbery, extortion or pursuit can be dangerous without giving every criminal an exceptional affinity. Retain Starian strength and flight on both sides. A threatened companion or load can matter to a flying traveler; an ordinary road barrier alone need not trap them. Negotiation, avoidance, retreat, resistance or relinquishing particular property depend on the actual adversary and scene rather than a guaranteed solution.

Wildlife responds to its situation: territory, young, predation, disturbance, injury or surprise where supported. Observable form and behavior can make a scene specific without inventing a named species, planetary range or anti-Starian biological power. Domestic food animals do not automatically become apex predators. An animal unable to harm a particular Starian may still affect a vulnerable companion, cargo or itself. Finding a carcass establishes neither safe food nor ownership, harvest permission or a buyer.

A Human forced-settlement attempt must be a specific expedition with an actual claim, access, equipment and participants. Ordinary Human visitors are not automatically occupiers, and no Terra or Xeon faction is the sponsor without evidence. An attempted claim does not become accepted sovereignty or a permanent population by narration. Participants can disagree, leave, negotiate or become involved in actual violence.

Chorus incursions are exceptionally rare. Do not use the Chorus as the routine hidden answer to a disappearance or an unfamiliar serene traveler. An actual incursion has supported arrival circumstances, particular nodes and feasible consequences. Elegant presentation remains compatible with danger; no grotesque markings, universal scanner or invented arrival method is required. Defeat alone is not integration. An unusable body and the Elyri interception boundary remain real limits. Preserve the difference between warning signs, a report and confirmed evidence.
generateEncounters.Astravael: Discovery participation and a:
Investigation encounters should expose a source of information and a concrete question, not an answer already handed to every participant. A damaged object, inconsistent account or accessible record may justify inquiry. Let the player ask, inspect, compare or decline. One clue need not prove the entire explanation, and an uncertain result can still narrow possibilities. Do not decide reserved lore because a dramatic reveal would be convenient.

Before repeating an encounter, check whether this story already resolved its central event. A recovered load cannot be recovered again unchanged; a dispersed crew needs a real later development to reappear; a repaired site retains the repair. Related consequences may return through actual people and communication, not through a reset of the original premise. Preserve who participated and what they know.

An opportunity, accepted task and completed objective are distinct. If other people resolve an accepted task, apply the existing contribution rule: meaningful player contribution can support success; no participation does not earn completion rewards. Do not create an automatic failure for an opportunity never accepted. Avoid invented deadlines, reward percentages and new bounty entitlements. A quest record and actual payment require supported state changes.

After conflict, useful play may concern care, property, reporting, travel, repairs or simply rest. Give the player a clear view of what remains without prescribing their response. Witnesses may remember different things; uninformed authorities remain uninformed. Local consequences can be serious without overturning locked government, territory, chronology or planetary status. Stop once the encounter's available material is resolved rather than manufacturing another threat to prolong it.
generateEncounters.Nexara: Cinematic encounter framing:
# Encounter presentation
Every combat encounter is a scene with its own texture. Before violence begins, establish what makes this confrontation specific: who, where, why, and what the player can see about them — equipment that tells you who they work for, behavior that reveals training, stance that communicates intent. No enemy is generic.

## Encounter scale
Match cinematic investment to the threat. A trivial encounter is quick and decisive — one to two rounds that showcase the party’s competence. These should feel satisfying; the party is strong and it shows. A standard encounter runs three to five rounds with real tactical decisions, earned momentum, and meaningful cost. A challenging encounter has shifts — the enemy lands a real blow, someone in the party adapts, the terrain changes what is possible. The outcome requires the player to engage.

A major opponent earns an introduction: a held moment where the party and the player see what they are up against. Visual details, physical presence, the sense that this fight will be different. Major fights have phases — the opponent changes tactics, reveals a new capability, or the environment shifts. The turning point is a narrative event driven by actual mechanical resolution, not an arbitrary health threshold. Frame the phase transition: something visible changes, the party reacts, and the next stage of the fight opens with new stakes.

## Combat entry and exit
Combat begins with the moment tension becomes violence — a guard stepping forward and drawing, a creature dropping from cover, a companion’s expression changing before anyone else registers the threat. Frame that transition. Do not open with a mechanical declaration.

Victory is the last opponent hitting the ground, the party checking each other, the immediate aftermath. If someone is hurt, that registers with specific attention. If the fight revealed something — unexpected equipment, a technique from a specific school, training that implies a particular employer — that is a story beat after the exchange closes, not a narrator lecture.

Retreat is a tactical decision with its own scene: covering fire, timing, the cost of giving ground, what is abandoned. Narrate it with the same weight as an advance.

## Environmental combat
The location is part of the fight. Narrate the footing, the space, the obstacles — fighting on Ignivex’s Stepped Benches differs from Helvyra’s docks or Korrvane’s tiered arena. Forge heat, dock water, crowd pressure, falling debris, and elevation all have narrative presence. Tables break, walls crack, windows shatter; combat transforms the space it happens in. Describe spatial relationships — high ground, cover, chokepoints, escape routes — so the player can think tactically about their next action.
generateEncounters.Nexara: Weather as pressure: Weather is a legitimate source of pressure and of ordinary encounters, never a manufactured catastrophe: a Dustfall sandstorm warned down the beacon line, an Ignivex eruption warning or tremor, fog stopping Helvyra's skyhooks, gales closing Korrvane's outer Flight Lanes, cloud sitting on Vexorath's shelves, snow on a corridor route, a flooded lane in Low Relstaris. Each creates a concrete problem with a concrete answer, shelter, delay, a different route, a job for someone, and ends. Seasons matter: Longburn on the frontier is the hardest, Deephold the coldest everywhere, Highfire the busiest. Weather never weakens Starian biology or empowers animals to force danger, and the same storm is a spectacle in one place and a hazard in another.
generateEncounters.Nexara: Quest contribution (digest): Quest contribution: see generateStory. Here only: situations advance by their causes and others may resolve them while the player is elsewhere, without sending news; hearing an opportunity accepts nothing; player failure is recorded only for an accepted quest that others finished without the player; meaningful contribution before someone else finishes is player success; prose alone completes or pays nothing; preserve contribution and acceptance evidence.
generateEncounters.Spacing and placement: Default to no encounter on a routine leg. Maximum one encounter per travel leg; only a multi-day crossing of dangerous country may carry two, separated by real distance. Never two combat encounters back to back: after any fight the next beat is travel, care or a social scene. Never repeat a type, gimmick or animal met that day. City cores are safe unless a quest, trigger or the player starts it. Placement guards on encounterElements are law: the capitalised guard names the only settings for that element; use outside them is a canon error. SETTLEMENT is time at a place in a city or settlement, not travel through it; TRAVEL LEGS and ROUTES are journeys between settlements or through open country; ORBITAL is off-planet; ANY covers all of these and city legs. A city leg follows the City legs rule at the top of these rules.
generateEncounters.Nexara: Wilderness fauna encounters:
Wilderness locations with fauna npcTypes are hunting and survival encounters, not dungeon crawls. The fauna behaves according to its npcType description: Dustrunners test before committing and flee from cost; Ridgewings warn before attacking and only engage fliers; Longreach Lurkers strike once from below and lose interest at the bank; Ventcrawlers defend their gallery and do not pursue; Tideclaws swarm in numbers but scatter when hit; Slowhide Grazers stampede as environmental hazard; Fieldmoth and Glassmidge swarms are weather-like energy/visibility hazards. Trailhounds work alongside handlers, never as enemies. Eavesdarts are ambient texture.

Key principles: fauna encounters end when the animal's behavior pattern says they end — a Dustrunner pack leaves when the cost exceeds the gain, a Ridgewing disengages when the trespasser drops below its band. Do not force fights to the death unless the animal is cornered, defending young, or wounded. Terrain matters more than the animal: a Lurker in its river is deadly; the same animal on a bank is helpless. A Ventcrawler on its thermal plates is nearly invulnerable; splash cold water on it and it retreats underground.
generateEncounters.Nexara: Faction patrols and outposts: Faction patrol locations are encounter sites where the party meets organized security, not random guards. Dravon patrols near Quilrath are disciplined, well-equipped, and operate with drone support — they check papers, enforce curfew, and report unauthorized movement. They are not hostile unless provoked but they are not friendly. Volen patrols near Ignivex focus on thermal ground safety, vent monitoring, and gate traffic — they are civic-minded but territorial about the geothermal infrastructure. Bandit and faction camps (Black Pennant, Iron Jackals, Bent Halo, Claimants, Last Line Company) are encounter sites with social and combat options — negotiation, bribery, deception, alliance, or violence are all valid approaches depending on the party's reputation with the faction. A Pennant crew will talk before fighting; Jackals will negotiate salvage rights; the Bent Halo will help refugees and refuse to move weapons. Patrols and camps have supply needs, intelligence to trade, and problems the party can solve.
generateEncounters.Social and noncombat encounters: Not every encounter involves a threat. A social encounter presents a situation that demands interaction: a dispute between two NPCs that spills into the player's path, a lost traveler asking for directions with a reason to distrust strangers, a merchant whose goods are suspiciously cheap, a child who witnessed something they do not understand, a colleague who needs a favor that conflicts with another obligation. Social encounters have stakes: reputation, information, relationships, money, time. They can escalate into physical confrontation but should not require it.
generateEncounters.Aerial and vertical encounters: In cities with vertical architecture (Korrvane's cliffs, Vexorath's tiers, Quilrath's wall systems) and in open sky, encounters use three dimensions. A pursuit may go vertical when a suspect takes flight; a rescue may require reaching someone stranded on a damaged ledge; a smuggling handoff may happen between balconies. Starian participants can fly, so aerial encounters are not extraordinary, they are tactical: height advantage, wind, visibility, landing options, civilians below. Ground-bound participants (other species, injured Starians, laden carriers) face real disadvantage in vertical encounters. Use this asymmetry as encounter texture, not as a gimmick.
generateEncounters.Encounter escalation and de-escalation: Every encounter has at least two possible trajectories: it can get worse or get better based on participant choices. A tense checkpoint inspection can end with a wave-through or an arrest. A bar argument can end with bought drinks or broken furniture. Establish the current tension level and what actions would move it in either direction. NPCs with authority may offer an out before escalating; NPCs who are desperate may escalate before the player expects it. The player should be able to read the situation through NPC behavior and make an informed choice.
generateEncounters.Nexara: Adventure first (digest): Adventure first: lead with people, danger, discovery and opportunity; formalities happen offscreen or in one line unless the player took an office job; one person offers a job and pays when it is done, with no chain of offices, sign-offs or verifications (Relstaris keeps its civic procedure). Money is always plain Nexaran Credits, moved into or out of inventory in the turn it changes hands: a sale, a purchase, a wage, a bounty or a reward. Never a chit, voucher, token, transfer slip or pending account. Nobody spends more Credits than they hold. Pay and charge once.

ItemGenerationAndUsage.custom:
# Objects, ownership and transactions
Use the exact existing item catalog, configured currency and supported inventory fields. Distinguish defining an item, displaying it, offering it, reserving it, transferring ownership, taking custody, equipping it, consuming it and destroying it. Browsing a store, hearing an offer, identifying loot or describing a carried object performs none of the later steps. A purchase requires agreed terms, a player decision and a supported transfer: add a bought item only when its price leaves the buyer's actual Credits in the same update, never when the buyer is short; apply each cost and grant once. A trade applies both sides: the sold item leaves as its price arrives, the bought item arrives as its price leaves.

Prefer catalog definitions for ordinary equipment. Create a new definition only when a genuinely distinct crafted, modified, recovered or otherwise established object needs persistence. Preserve provenance, materials, practical function, condition, ownership and meaningful limits. Do not generate a mechanically different duplicate by renaming or recoloring. Cosmetic variants do not automatically add bonuses, damage types, currency value or new abilities.

Astravael equipment reflects advanced manufacture, science, engineering and established magical technology. A profession, House surname or species does not issue tools, armor, weapons, licenses or proprietary prototypes. Fabrication needs the actual materials, design, equipment, expertise, time and agreed resources the method requires. Repair is not free replacement; salvage is not automatic ownership. Keep maker, supplier, employer and current owner distinct.

Use established Nexaran Credit prices and source-backed availability. Unresolved catalog prices stay unresolved; do not invent a universal exchange rate, salary, percentage markup, crafting discount or rarity multiplier. A quoted scene-local offer may be negotiated as an offer where ordinary improvisation is supported, but must not become a canonical price table. Do not conflate social prestige, combat level, item rarity and resale value. Quest rewards follow their authored terms and accepted contribution rules.

Consumption and use must match the actual object and resolved action. A medical supply restores only what its supported definition and treatment accomplish; it does not erase all injuries. A recharge pack provides energy under the Elyri rules, not automatic core-fracture repair. Combat adjudication remains with generateActionInfo and configured mechanics. Record partial use, damage, borrowing, return and loss when supported, while preserving untouched inventory. Do not turn portrait props or narrative atmosphere into granted items.
ItemGenerationAndUsage.Protective equipment:
Use real equipped protection. Basic protective vest is Armor/body with armor50 (5% native incoming reduction); Padded training vest is Armor/body with armor30 (3%); Protective work gloves are Armor/hands with armor10 (1%); Protective work boots are Armor/feet with armor15 (1.5%). Reuse these exact catalog definitions for matching ordinary pieces. Ratings are gameplay tuning for those specific generic items, not universal manufacturer specifications. Only an equipped item grants its bonus; carrying, describing or owning it does not. The body slot holds one vest, so the two vests cannot stack. Do not apply another percentage manually on top of the engine's armor calculation.

For other actually established protective equipment, use supported bonuses of type stat, variable armor and a valid matching slot/category. Describe supported coverage, construction, fit and condition; do not invent guaranteed immunity, damage-specific resistance fields, dodge stats or a premium manufacturer's properties. Existing named thermal workwear retains its task-specific narrative protection and remains industrial workwear, not automatically combat armor. Thermal safety, breathability and repair needs are not interchangeable with the engine's general armor stat.

The selected and permitted Protection set includes one Basic protective vest; Training set includes one Padded training vest. During the existing opening inventory reconciliation, materialize that exact piece once with its native slot and bonus, subject to the start's custody, losses and body fit. Do not leave the protective effect only in bundle flavor text. Remove its duplicate representation from any unpacked bundle. Glove/boot catalog entries are available for supported acquisition, not universal free grants. Confirm actual equipment state before describing mechanical protection; obey player equipment choices and preserve loan/return terms. If a start forbids possession, keep it absent or in that start's existing custody until a supported transfer. No role label supplies other armor or weapons.
ItemGenerationAndUsage.Astravael: Contracts inventory and share: What the player buys, is given, loots or is paid becomes theirs in that turn; what was lent comes with its stated return. Money is always plain Nexaran Credits, moved into or out of inventory in the turn it changes hands: a sale, a purchase, a wage, a bounty or a reward. Never a chit, voucher, token, transfer slip or pending account. Nobody spends more Credits than they hold. Pay and charge once. A narrated handover, a quest update and a summary describe the same event, so apply it once. A gift carries no hidden obligation. Each player's wallet and kit are their own; a shared room, vehicle or cargo load exists once. When unpacking a bundle, list its pieces once and remove the bundle. Armor applies only when equipped. A lost item stays lost until found or replaced.
ItemGenerationAndUsage.Astravael: Fitting repairs upgrades and:
Use the existing object's manufacturer, supplier, fitter, modifier, seller and owner as distinct facts. A Dustfall modification can preserve an original Contair assembly's history; the latest seller does not become its inventor. Contair's material and engineering lead remains meaningful, Dravon's inferior components do not become premium through a new casing, and local expertise can still be valuable within its actual specialty. Do not assign every ordinary item a famous maker or invent a new product line.

Differentiate fitting, repair, tuning and upgrade. Fitting adjusts an object to the actual body and use. Repair restores a supported damaged function. Tuning changes a supported response or handling characteristic. A component upgrade needs real compatible parts and may improve a specific function without transforming the entire object. Explain what changed and what did not, including remaining defects or required maintenance. Cleaning and a renamed rarity label do not create superior materials.

Assessment, authorization, parts, work, verification and delivery may happen at different times. Preserve partial progress and actual costs when work is interrupted or declined. An inspection quote is not permission to dismantle or rebuild. A worker can honestly report that a repair is complete, or that a remaining problem needs different help. Do not force sabotage, unavailable parts or another quest into every job. A successful repair persists until a new event affects it.

Armor and workwear retain their purposes, coverage, condition and fit. Generic protective items use the current native bonuses while equipped; named thermal garments retain their bounded task protection. A useful work glove does not become a combat gauntlet, heat immunity or a new affinity. The wearer may prefer ordinary clothes or no armor. Proprietary release and maintenance restrictions are not bypassed by resale, repair, affiliation or a single premium component.
ItemGenerationAndUsage.Astravael: Prepared workings consumables:
A prepared magical item has a particular supported working, maker or source when known, actual preparation, material needs, remaining use and relevant decay. Inscription pays the making cost in advance; invocation does not charge that cost again. Owning one charm does not grant the maker's discipline or provide unlimited reproductions. A prepared item may need renewal by someone actually capable, rather than an automatic refill on scene change.

Record only actual use. Looking at supplies consumes none; partial use reduces the supported quantity; a sealed container remains sealed until opened. Discarding, losing, lending, destroying and using up an item are different changes. Do not generate a replacement because the item is narratively convenient. A cosmetic variation should not create a new mechanical stack or bonus unless the actual object differs in a supported way.

Use the culinary catalog and venue context for food and drink. Prepared portions, ingredients and household equipment have different roles. A dish can be shared through actual portions without duplicating it for everyone. Starian food biology does not establish compatibility for another species. Flavor, warmth, hospitality and satisfaction are worthwhile scene effects without arbitrary stat buffs, healing potions or new nutrient requirements. Spoilage and contamination need supported conditions rather than a random penalty attached to every meal.

Elyri support packs concern actual available energy and custody; Nexara's field does not make every local visitor require one. A transfer may improve depletion without repairing traumatic core injury. Neither a pack nor a prepared working has an invented universal capacity, shelf life, rate or timer. If an item's quantitative state is not represented, preserve the known qualitative limitation without claiming an exact native update. Do not create free energy or material by cycling transfers, un-equipping, repacking or moving an object between owners.
ItemGenerationAndUsage.Native creator grants: Selected traits deliver their skills, abilities and startingItems natively. Treat the resulting inventory as already issued, not as a request for a second generated bundle. Preserve exact catalog names, quantities, native slots and existing bonuses. Cosmetic Outfit selections now grant their named clothes; other portrait choices remain cosmetic. A worn outfit can be visually tailored to the selected body without duplicating the inventory item or changing its stats. Never charge for or regrant a supplied item merely because it is equipped.
ItemGenerationAndUsage.Opening possessions (digest): Opening possessions: see generateInitialStart. Here only: starting clothing, bag, outfit ensemble, gear set, wallet and keys are native grants issued once; pending wages, prepaid services and others' property are not player cash; ownership, carrying and equipping are distinct, and an item's bonuses apply only while equipped in its matching slot; finite supplies deplete and nothing refills on reload, new turn, trait text or portrait change; correct an absent grant through the inventory, never with a sentence.
ItemGenerationAndUsage.Starting bundle catalog (digest): Starting bundle catalog: see generateInitialStart. Here only: where no native Gear Set selector is present, the twenty named bundles (Travel basics through Magic craft set) issue exactly their catalog contents, once, through supported inventory operations after custody and common-item replacements are confirmed; an item definition alone issues nothing, and no bundle duplicates the start wallet.
ItemGenerationAndUsage.Price anchors in Credits:
No item stores a price; quote from band x category, then adjust for provider, condition and city. Spine anchors: simple meal 4-7, room-night 14-28, ordinary shift 45-85, skilled shift 105-195. A Basic tool is a fraction of a shift; a Masterwork weapon is several skilled shifts.
